Mail is now postmarked when the post office processes it, not when you drop it off, so a hand-stamp at a post office counter or an early mailing is the safer route. Returned checks carry a $25 fee.

Late payment and delinquent taxes

Unpaid tax carries 1.5% interest for each month or part of a month, under 35 ILCS 200/21-15. The payment scale on each stub shows the penalty for each date range. Under 35 ILCS 200/21-135 the collector also adds $10 for certified mailing, advertising and publication costs.

  • 35 ILCS 200/20-25 lets the collector refuse a personal or corporate check within 45 days before a tax sale.
  • Unpaid parcels are published and certified letters go out. Then the Treasurer takes judgment from the circuit court and runs the delinquent tax sale.
  • The County Clerk figures rates and collects redemptions on sold taxes.

Ask the Treasurer for a payoff figure by parcel number before any closing. The county's online property tax inquiry searches by parcel number, owner name, address, sale price or tax code, and prints the bill and payment history for each parcel.

How to appeal your assessment

Start by asking the township assessor or the county deputy assessors for an informal review, then file a complaint with the Board of Review if needed. The 30-day complaint window opens when your township's notice runs in the newspaper, and that date moves every year. A tax bill itself can't be appealed. After it arrives, only errors of fact, such as a missing exemption or wrong square footage, can be fixed through the Assessment Office.

The Board of Review rules matter if you're in the middle of a sale. The person filing must hold a legal interest at the time: a recorded deed, a recorded contract for deed or installment memorandum, or a purchase agreement fully signed by both parties. Complaints go in by hand, or by mail, courier or parcel service postmarked on or before the last filing day. Email and fax are refused.

  • Equity appeals compare similar nearby homes. Market value appeals rest on recent sales of comparable homes.
  • Useful evidence includes a realtor's market analysis, a certified appraisal, a comparable sheet, a closing statement and photographs.
  • After a tentative decision and a hearing, a final notice goes out. From that notice's postmark, you have 30 days to go to the Illinois Property Tax Appeal Board.
Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Fulton County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Homestead and other exemptions

Fulton County lists seven homestead exemptions, and the owner has to apply for each one. Check your bill every year to confirm you're getting all you qualify for.

  • General Homestead Exemption for owner-occupied residences
  • Senior Citizen Homestead Exemption for owners over 65
  • Senior Citizens Assessment Freeze Exemption, which holds assessed value at a base year, with income limits. It does not freeze the tax bill amount.
  • Homestead Improvement Exemption for value added by a new improvement on a parcel that also has the general exemption
  • Returning Veteran's, Disabled Veteran's (at least 50% service-connected disability certified by the VA) and Disabled Persons' exemptions

A new owner-occupant should ask the Assessment Office, extension 113, which filings are needed once the deed is recorded. A seller who moved out midyear can ask the same office how that year's exemption is handled.

Selling with unpaid or unclear tax

Begin with the parcel number, printed at the top left of the bill and searchable online. Work through these steps:

  • Pull the payment history and confirm which installments are open.
  • Ask the Treasurer for the total owed with penalties through the expected closing date, and get it in writing.
  • Take the Assessment Office any exemption that should be on the parcel, since an error of fact can be corrected after the bill is issued.
  • Give the title company the payoff so the tax is paid from proceeds at closing.

A house with deferred repairs, back taxes or an estate attached can sit on the market where values are this modest. Some owners choose a direct as-is sale to a cash buyer, which skips repairs and puts the tax settlement into the contract. On any route, the written payoff is what keeps the closing on schedule.

Frequently asked questions

When are Fulton County property taxes due?

In two installments, with dates that change yearly. The 2024 taxes payable in 2025 were due June 13 and September 5. The stubs on your current bill carry the live dates, or call (309) 547-3041, extension 132.

Who sends the Fulton County tax bill?

The County Treasurer, who is also ex-officio County Collector, prints and mails it. The County Clerk works out the rates and the Assessor sets values and approves exemptions. If nothing arrives, call the Treasurer anyway.

What is the penalty for paying Fulton County taxes late?

Interest of 1.5% accrues for each month or part of a month, under 35 ILCS 200/21-15. A $10 mailing and publication charge applies under 35 ILCS 200/21-135, and each stub prints a scale of amounts by date range.

How long do Fulton County owners have to appeal an assessment?

Thirty days from the newspaper publication for your township, and that date shifts yearly. File with the Supervisor of Assessments by hand or postmarked mail. The Property Tax Appeal Board has its own 30-day clock from the final notice's postmark.

Can someone under contract to buy a Fulton County house file an assessment complaint?

Yes, if the purchase agreement is fully signed by both parties. The Board of Review also accepts a recorded deed, a recorded installment memorandum or a contract for deed as a qualifying legal interest.

Grundy County, IL Property Tax Guide: Offices, Appeals and Selling With Tax Due

Cash Home Buyers in Illinois

Who collects Grundy County property tax

The Grundy County Treasurer, acting as County Collector, mails and collects the bills from the courthouse at 111 E. Washington Street in Morris. The Supervisor of Assessments oversees values, administers exemptions and acts as clerk to the Board of Review. That office doesn't collect tax, calculate it or set the rate, so questions about the dollar amount on a bill belong with the Treasurer and the taxing districts.

  • Seventeen townships: Aux Sable, Braceville, Erienna, Felix, Garfield, Goodfarm, Goose Lake, Greenfield, Highland, Maine, Mazon, Morris, Nettle Creek, Norman, Saratoga, Vienna and Wauponsee
  • Villages include Braceville, Carbon Hill, Gardner, Kinsman, Mazon, South Wilmington and Verona, plus parts of Channahon, Coal City, Dwight, Minooka and Seneca

Grundy County housing at a glance

Grundy County is part of the Chicago metropolitan area, and Morris is both the seat and the biggest city. It's one of the faster-growing and higher-priced counties around. Population is 54,052, up 2.8% from the 2020 base, in 21,652 housing units, and owners hold 74.4% of occupied homes. The median owner-occupied home value is $271,700, monthly ownership cost with a mortgage is $2,016 and median household income is $92,235.

At those values, a late installment carries a penalty that grows every month it sits. Anyone who inherited a house or fell behind on payments should find out the open balance early.

Due dates and payment deadlines

Grundy County bills one year behind and sends bills in two installments. For the 2025 taxes payable in 2026, bills were mailed by late May, the first installment fell on a Friday in late June and the second on a Friday in early September. Mobile home bills have their own August due date. Schedules differ from one tax year to the next, so confirm the year you're closing in with the Treasurer's office.

Grundy County payment rules by date
Date or periodPayment rule
Through October 15Electronic checks accepted
October 1 and laterCash, cashier's check, credit card or money order only; no personal or business checks; $10 publication fee added to delinquent parcels
Through October 31Major credit cards accepted
Any late payment1.5% penalty per month under Illinois law

Card payments carry a 2.5% convenience fee with a $3 minimum, and e-checks a $1.50 flat fee, both kept by the payment processor.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Grundy County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Where to pay

The Treasurer takes payment online, by mail, by phone at 815-324-6390, in the drop box outside the Sheriff's Department, at participating local banks and in person at the courthouse.

The county's Property Tax Inquiry Portal lets an owner or buyer search a parcel, review payment history, see the current amount due and pull up assessment data. Look there before you accept an offer, so you know whether either installment is still open.

The annual tax sale

Unpaid taxes are sold at an annual tax sale in early November at the Grundy County Administration Building, 1320 Union Street in Morris. Under Illinois Public Act 104-0553 and a standing direction of the County Board, the Treasurer will sell all legally eligible delinquent liens or certificates at future sales to Grundy County as Trustee for the taxing districts.

That transfer moves the tax lien or certificate, not immediate title to the house. If the taxes on a parcel were sold, the owner redeems by paying the unpaid tax plus fees at the County Clerk's office. A seller whose taxes went to sale should have the redemption amount from the County Clerk, quoted by parcel number, before a closing is scheduled.

How to appeal your assessment

Assessment notices go out in September, and the complaint deadline falls in late October at 4:30 pm. Complaints can be filed in person, by email to the Board of Review address, or by mail postmarked by 11:59 pm on deadline day. Each year's assessment feeds the tax bills mailed the following year.

The Board of Review publishes equalized assessed values in two newspapers. The Coal City Courant covers Braceville, Felix, Garfield, Goodfarm, Goose Lake, Greenfield and Maine townships, and the Morris Herald-News covers Aux Sable, Erienna, Highland, Mazon, Morris, Nettle Creek, Norman, Saratoga, Vienna and Wauponsee. Starting with tax year 2026, no notice is mailed when a parcel changed only by the equalization factor or state farmland values. Those owners should check the online Assessment Inquiry using the parcel number without dashes.

  • The Board of Review assesses omitted property, hears written complaints, equalizes between property classes, hears exemption requests and issues certificates of error.
  • Forms and the yearly rules and procedures are on the Board of Review page of the county website.
  • Decisions can be taken to the Illinois Property Tax Appeal Board, and then to the courts.
Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Grundy County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Exemptions and relief programs

The county's Property Tax Relief page describes the state programs and the form each needs. Applications go to the chief county assessment office, except the deferral, which runs through the Treasurer.

  • General Homestead Exemption: for a principal residence, with a maximum $6,000 reduction in EAV
  • Senior Citizens Homestead Exemption: $5,000 off EAV for owners 65 or older
  • Senior Citizens Assessment Freeze Exemption: form PTAX-340 each year, with a household income cap
  • Disabled Persons Homestead Exemption: $2,000 off EAV. Returning veteran: $5,000 off EAV.
  • Disabled veteran standard exemption: $2,500 for 30% to 49% disability, $5,000 for 50% to 69%, and full exemption at 70% or more
  • Homestead Improvement Exemption: up to $75,000 for four years after the improvement is occupied

The senior deferral covers owners aged 65 and up with household income below $55,000. The state pays the tax, records a lien, and collects the money back with 6% annual interest once the house is sold or transferred, so a sale ends the deferral. The Assessment Office can state the current income limit for the freeze.

Selling with tax due

Take these steps before you set a closing date:

  • Look the parcel up in the Property Tax Inquiry Portal and note which installments show as paid.
  • Ask the Treasurer for a total through the target closing date.
  • If a deferral lien is on the parcel, get a recovery balance. If taxes were sold, get a redemption figure from the County Clerk.
  • Keep every payoff figure in writing and hand copies to the title company.

Even with strong values, a house that needs repairs or carries a tax problem can stall. Selling as is to a cash buyer skips repair negotiations, and the open balance gets settled in the purchase contract.

Frequently asked questions

When is the second Grundy County property tax installment due?

The second installment falls on a Friday in early September, and the first on a Friday in late June. The Treasurer's page carries the exact schedule for each tax year.

Can I pay Grundy County property tax with a personal check in October?

No. From October 1 the Treasurer accepts only cash, a cashier's check, a credit card or a money order. E-checks stop after October 15 and cards after October 31, and a $10 publication fee is added to delinquent parcels.

What does the Grundy County tax sale transfer to the buyer?

A tax lien or certificate, not title to the house. The county, acting as Trustee for the taxing districts, buys eligible liens at future sales. The owner redeems by paying the unpaid tax and fees at the County Clerk's office.

Who handles Grundy County exemption applications?

The Supervisor of Assessments administers homestead and non-homestead exemptions. Organizations seeking a non-homestead exemption apply through the Board of Review. Forms are on the county's assessor forms page.

How much is the penalty for late Grundy County property tax?

It's 1.5% a month under Illinois law. Delinquent parcels also pick up a $10 publication fee after October 1. The Treasurer can quote an exact payoff for your parcel and date.

Henry County offices and contacts

The Treasurer and the Assessment Office share the building at 307 W. Center Street in Cambridge, the county seat. The County Clerk files the levies and extends the tax to each parcel, usually finishing in April, and then the Treasurer prints and mails the bills. The Board of Review has three citizen members named by the County Board chair, and the Chief County Assessor is its clerk.

  • Treasurer: 309-937-3576, open Monday through Friday from 8 am to 4:30 pm except holidays
  • Assessment Office: 309-937-3570, open Monday through Friday from 8 am to 4:30 pm
  • Cities: Colona, Galva, Geneseo and Kewanee. Villages include Alpha, Andover, Bishop Hill, Cambridge, Cleveland, Orion and Woodhull.

Henry County housing at a glance

Henry County is a mostly agricultural county in northwest Illinois, in the Davenport-Moline-Rock Island metro area, with Kewanee its largest city. Its housing is older and owner-heavy. Population is 48,095, down 2.4% from the 2020 base, with 22,199 housing units and owners in 79.9% of homes. The median owner-occupied home is valued at $151,600. Median gross rent is $842 and median household income is $71,911.

Tax roll and new construction

The Assessment Office handles just over 31,000 parcels with a total assessed value of $1,535,199,680. The levy process draws on 124 taxing districts, 23 drainage districts and 27 TIF districts. Districts file their requests on the last Tuesday in December, and the Clerk checks them against the Truth-in-Taxation law and statutory rate limits.

Property is valued as of January 1 each year. For new construction, the statute makes the January 1 owner liable, on a proportionate basis, for the added tax from the date the occupancy permit issued or the improvement became fit for use through December 31. If you finished an addition last year, ask the Assessment Office how that proration affects your next bill.

Due dates

Henry County bills in two installments. For tax year 2025 payable 2026, the due dates were in June and September. Ask the Treasurer for the dates that apply to the tax year you're closing in, and read the bill itself, since banks can't take payment after the second due date.

Paying your bill

Henry County accepts payment by card, e-check, mail, drop box, in person, through local banks and by automatic withdrawal. Cards cost 2.25% plus $1.50 per transaction and e-checks $2, paid to the processor. The courthouse drop box takes everything except cash.

Henry County payment programs and limits
ProgramTerms
Automatic withdrawal (ACH)Debits on the first and second due dates; form must arrive 10 business days before a due date
Pre-paymentsDecember 1 to April 1; must be current on prior taxes; up to the previous year's amount only

Local banksEight banks accept bills with the full statement; not after the second due date

With pre-payments, the bill later shows the remaining balance or a refund owed on overages once bills are generated. Money paid in advance can't be pulled back before then.

What happens to unpaid taxes

Unpaid taxes become delinquent, and the Treasurer runs a sale of them every year. Tax buyers, professional and private, bid for the right to buy the delinquent amount, and the winner pays the outstanding tax. You don't lose the house right away. Owners have two and a half years to redeem, after which the buyer may grant an extension or petition the Circuit Court for a tax deed.

  • Original interest on a sold tax can run from 0% to 18% annually, plus court costs, certified mailing and other fees.
  • Redemption goes through the County Clerk. Bring the parcel number, because the amount owed depends on the day.
  • Redemption must be paid in full by cash, money order or bank cashier's check. Illinois law doesn't allow personal checks or credit cards for it.

If you're selling a house whose taxes were sold, ask the Clerk for the redemption figure early.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Henry County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Assessment appeals and the senior freeze

The Chief County Assessor equalizes values and publishes changes between October 15 and November 15 each year. The Board of Review accepts appeals for 30 days after publication. If the Board's written decision doesn't satisfy you, you have 30 days from the date of that notice to go to the Illinois Property Tax Appeal Board. Splits and combinations of parcels must be requested by September 30.

Get the Board of Review complaint form from the Assessment Office. The Board checks whether the township assessor and county assessor calculated values correctly. It can equalize assessments, add omitted property, rule on homestead exemptions and review non-homestead exemption applications.

  • The senior freeze income limit rose from $65,000 to $75,000. An owner with income at or under $75,000 who has never qualified can file the form on the county site or call the office.
  • Freeze forms are mailed each January to everyone who qualified the year before.
  • Ask the Assessment Office for the residential exemption applications.

Selling with tax due at closing

Here is the order that keeps a Henry County closing on track:

  • Open the county's Property Tax Inquiry site with the parcel number and read the bill and payment status.
  • Phone the Treasurer at 309-937-3576 for a payoff figure through the planned closing date, and ask which installments are still open for the year of closing.
  • Call the Clerk if any year was sold at the delinquent sale.
  • Get every payoff in writing for the title company.

Pre-payments are worth knowing about if you list in winter or spring. The program lets a current-on-taxes owner send money ahead of the bills, and the remaining balance or any refund shows up once the new bills are generated. Tell the title company about any pre-payment so the closing statement credits it correctly. If the buyer will take over an automatic withdrawal, remember the form has to reach the Treasurer 10 business days before a due date, so the new owner should file their own.

With a countywide median value of $151,600, an old tax debt or a repair bill is a heavy share of what many houses here are worth. Selling as is to a cash buyer is one way to skip repairs and settle the tax in the purchase contract, as long as the payoffs are confirmed in writing first.

Frequently asked questions

When are Henry County property taxes due?

In two installments. For tax year 2025 payable 2026, they were due in June and September. The Treasurer posts the dates for each year on the Treasurer page of the county website.

Can a Henry County bank take my property tax after the second due date?

No. Banks can't accept payments after the second due date. After that, the Treasurer's office is where you pay, and a delinquent bill can go to the annual sale.

How long can a Henry County owner redeem sold taxes?

Two and a half years. After that the tax buyer may extend the time or petition the Circuit Court for a tax deed. Redemption goes through the County Clerk in cash, money order or cashier's check only.

How long do I have to appeal a Henry County assessment?

Thirty days after assessments are published, which happens between October 15 and November 15. A further appeal to the Illinois Property Tax Appeal Board must be filed within 30 days of the Board of Review's written decision.

Does Henry County offer a way to pay property tax early?

Yes, a pre-payment program runs from December 1 to April 1. You must be current on prior-year taxes and may pay up to the previous year's amount only. A form is filled out each year at the time of payment.

Iroquois County tax offices

Two offices in the Iroquois County Administrative Center, 1001 East Grant Street in Watseka, share the work. The Treasurer is in Room 105 at (815) 432-6985, and bills the tax and takes payment. The Assessment Office, in Room 106 at (815) 432-6978, handles values, exemptions and appeals. Both are open weekdays and close at half past four.

A three-member Board of Review sits apart from the assessor's staff and decides complaints on the evidence shown at the hearing. Township assessors handle first-line questions about a parcel's record.

  • Bills, payments and tax sale questions: the County Treasurer
  • Exemptions, property record cards and address changes: the Assessment Office, where deputy clerks answer record requests by email
  • Assessment complaints: the Board of Review, using the county's complaint form
  • Tax rates: the County Clerk's Office

Iroquois County housing at a glance

Iroquois County lies along the Indiana line in northeast Illinois, with its northern edge about 60 miles south of Chicago. Watseka is the seat and the largest city, and Gilman is the other city. Interstate 57 runs along the western side, and U.S. Route 24 crosses the county from Gilman through Watseka to Sheldon. With 26 townships, the assessor for a parcel depends on its location, so check the township printed on the bill.

Population is 26,150, down from 27,077 in 2020, with 12,780 housing units and 80.0 percent of occupied homes owned by the people living in them. The median owner-occupied home is valued at $137,800, median gross rent is $799 and median household income is $66,255. Nearly a quarter of residents are 65 or older, so many owners here are thinking about downsizing or settling an estate.

Due dates and penalties

The two installment dates are announced each year when bills are mailed, and they've moved around. In one recent year the first installment fell in June, in another in August. The dates on your own bill govern. A late balance picks up 1 1/2 percent for every month it sits unpaid.

Each bill is paid the year after its tax year, so 2022 taxes are payable in 2023. Ask the treasurer for a written statement listing every year still owing, and pass it to your title company.

A member of a United States Armed Forces Reserve unit called to active duty outside the continental United States may defer an installment until 180 days after returning.

Ways to pay

You can pay at the treasurer's office in Room 105, by mail, at a participating bank or online through the county's property tax search page. Online, enter the parcel number without dashes, the owner name or the address, and a Pay Taxes button appears.

Iroquois County payment methods

Participating banksIncludes 1st Trust and Savings Bank in Watseka and Clifton, Iroquois Federal, Iroquois Farmers State Bank, Prospect Bank, First State Bank of Forrest and Commonwealth Credit UnionNo fee listed

Send or bring the whole bill. A $1.00 fee applies to payments made without it, and a receipt requires the full bill, with a stamped envelope if mailed. Mortgage companies must pay online. If a lender escrows your tax, confirm which year it paid before you order a payoff.

How to appeal your assessment

Complaints go to the Board of Review within 30 days of your township's assessment publication. Each township's cutoff is posted on the board's web page, and talking with a township assessor does not stop the clock.

The board's yearly session opens by the first Monday of June and continues day to day as needed. A reduction applies to the current assessment year only, except for omitted property. File all your evidence with the complaint itself, since the rules don't let you add it afterward.

  • Strong exhibits are an appraisal, comparable sales, the settlement statement from a recent purchase and current photographs.
  • An Illinois attorney must file for property held by an LLC, partnership or corporation.
  • If you disagree with the written decision, you have 30 calendar days to go to the state Property Tax Appeal Board, or you may object in circuit court under 35 ILCS 200/23-5.

The board may adjust a value up as well as down. Reassessment happens every four years, and the target is one-third of fair cash value.

Homestead exemption and other relief

The general homestead exemption removes up to $6,000 from the equalized assessed value of an owner-occupied home before tax is figured, under 35 ILCS 200/15-175. The application asks for a state driver's license or ID showing the home address, and after first approval the exemption renews automatically. If the home stops being your main residence, you must have the exemption taken off.

Other homestead exemptions run through the county too:

  • Returning veteran, disabled persons and disabled veteran (sections 15-167 to 15-169)
  • Senior citizens over 65 (section 15-170) and the senior assessment freeze (section 15-172)
  • The homestead improvements exemption (section 15-180)

To keep the bill correct, applications should reach the assessment office before the assessment year ends on December 31. The low-income senior freeze has its own filing window, January 1 through July 1. The treasurer also publicizes a senior property tax deferral program that works as a loan with interest, repaid when the property is sold or after the owner's death. Ask for current terms, since any deferral comes due at a sale.

If taxes go unpaid

Unpaid parcels can be sold to a tax buyer at the annual sale, and the treasurer's page carries buyer information and a registration form. A tax buyer doesn't take your house at the sale. The buyer gets a lien position and the right to petition for a deed if the owner never redeems.

Under 35 ILCS 200/21-350, redemption stays open for 3 years after the sale for certificates issued from January 1, 2024 onward, subject to exceptions that start with vacant property. Redemption payments go to the county clerk, who can give the exact deadline and payoff for a parcel that was sold.

Getting ready to sell

County records and your closing date need to line up, so start with the paper trail.

  • Get the parcel record and compare the owner name and mailing address against your deed.
  • Collect the treasurer's payoff figure for each year with an unpaid balance.
  • Learn which exemption should be dropped from the parcel after the sale.
  • See whether the Board of Review has an open complaint on your parcel.
  • Gather repair quotes if the house will be sold in its present state.

An as-is cash purchase is possible for an Iroquois County house, with any unpaid tax cleared in the settlement.

Frequently asked questions

What are the Iroquois County installment dates?

They change each year and are printed on the bill. In recent years the first installment has landed in June or August, with a 1 1/2 percent monthly penalty after each date.

Where can Iroquois County taxes be paid?

At the treasurer's counter at 1001 East Grant Street in Watseka, by mail, at a participating county bank, on the online property tax search page or in the after-hours drop box.

How long is the Iroquois County appeal window?

Thirty days from publication of the township's assessments. Each township's date is posted on the Board of Review page, and talking with the assessor does not extend it.

What does the Iroquois County general homestead exemption remove?

Up to $6,000 comes off the equalized assessed value under 35 ILCS 200/15-175. File through the Assessment Office, Room 106, with a license or ID that shows the home address.

Which Iroquois County phone number answers tax questions?

Use (815) 432-6985 for the Treasurer and (815) 432-6978 for the Assessment Office. Rates are a County Clerk matter.

Where to pay

Jackson County takes payments online, by phone, by mail, at banks and at the counter. Online card and e-check payments go through Municipay, and the phone line for card payments is 618-492-4566. The courthouse drop box is at the top of the accessible ramp on the Chestnut Street side, for checks or certified funds only.

  • By mail: Jackson County Treasurer, P.O. Box 430, Murphysboro, IL 62966-0430
  • At a bank: most Jackson County banks take payments on or before each installment date, but not mobile home payments
  • Convenience charges: cards cost 2.5 percent, never less than $2.00, and an e-check costs $1
  • Prepaying: the treasurer lets you make estimated monthly payments toward the next bill, interest free

Your parcel number (PIN) is on the Property Tax Inquiry page, or the treasurer can give it to you by phone.

Where the tax money goes

The county's explanatory page shows how 2024 taxes payable in 2025 were split among districts, and schools take most of it.

  • All schools: 63.69 percent
  • County purposes: 19.01 percent
  • Cities, villages and incorporated towns: 7.37 percent
  • Townships and road districts: 4.75 percent, and park districts 2.39 percent
  • Airport, fire protection, conservancy, library and other districts share the remaining fraction

Assessed value is meant to be 33 1/3 percent of market value, apart from farmland and farm buildings. The 2025 assessment notice put the required level at 33.33 percent and the countywide median level at 29.08 percent. Each district's levy and any exemptions then set the dollars, so two houses of similar value can get different bills.

How to appeal your assessment

Appeals go to the Board of Review within 30 days after the Supervisor of Assessments publishes a township's values. Publication generally comes in the fall, and the board's FAQ says no extensions are possible.

The board looks at value alone. A high bill, a steep percentage increase or a neighbor's smaller bill doesn't qualify by itself. Overvaluation, equity, physical data errors and preferential assessment are the four recognized reasons.

  • Each parcel needs its own form plus evidence, such as a recent appraisal, a settlement statement from the past two years or a comparison grid.
  • Owners or their attorneys file. Partnerships, LLCs and corporations must use an Illinois attorney.
  • Hearings are generally by teleconference or phone, and failing to attend can get an appeal dismissed.
  • If you reject the proposed decision, you have 10 days to request a hearing, then 30 days from the final decision to go to the Property Tax Appeal Board.

When a hearing is set after a due date, the county advises paying what's due and taking any refund later. A taxpayer who still objects pays under protest and files a tax objection complaint with the Circuit Clerk. A certificate of error corrects factual mistakes, like wrong square footage, but only on the current bill and before the annual tax sale.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Jackson County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

When taxes go unpaid

First comes a certified letter, then newspaper publication of the unpaid parcel, then the annual sale of the tax. Buyers bid an interest rate between 0 and 9 percent. The sale auctions the unpaid tax, not the house.

The county's explanation puts the point at which a tax buyer can petition for a deed at 30 months without redemption. Section 21-350 of the statute sets 3 years for certificates issued from January 1, 2024, so ask the County Clerk which period fits your parcel. If no buyer bids, the tax goes to the Jackson County Trustee, and a deed the Trustee obtains goes to an annual sealed bid auction where the buyer isn't responsible for the back taxes.

The County Clerk, at 618-687-7360, handles redemption of prior-year taxes.

Checklist before listing

Work through these before you take an offer:

  • Print the tax history from the lookup page and see which installments were paid.
  • Ask the treasurer for a payoff when a penalty is accruing or a tax sale date is near.
  • Ask the assessment office how to remove your owner-occupied exemption once you move.
  • Ask the Board of Review whether an appeal on the parcel is still pending.
  • Photograph the defects a buyer may price in.

A Jackson County house can be sold as is for cash, and any tax balance is settled at closing.

Frequently asked questions

What were the Jackson County installment dates for 2025 taxes?

September 4 and November 4, 2026. A 1 1/2 percent penalty applies for each month or part of a month after an installment date.

Where does the Jackson County Treasurer work?

In the courthouse at 1001 Walnut Street, Murphysboro, on weekdays until 4. The phone number is 618-687-7350.

When is the Jackson County appeal window?

Thirty days after the Supervisor of Assessments publishes your township's values, usually in the fall. The board doesn't grant extensions.

What does paying Jackson County taxes online cost?

Payments go through Municipay. Cards add 2.5 percent, never less than $2.00, and e-checks add $1.

Who processes redemption of back taxes in Jackson County?

The County Clerk, 618-687-7360, who can quote the redemption amount and deadline for a given parcel.

Cash Home Buyers in Illinois

Jefferson County tax offices

Mt. Vernon, the seat of Jefferson County in southern Illinois, is where a seller does most of the paperwork, at two courthouse desks. The Treasurer/Collector is at 100 South 10th Street, Room 100, Mt. Vernon, at 618-244-8010, closed by 4 p.m. on weekdays. In the same building, the Assessor (formally the Supervisor of Assessments) answers at 618-244-8016 and also serves as clerk to the Board of Review, so appeals and exemption forms live in one place.

The Treasurer's page lists what that office can't do, which makes a handy call guide:

  • Mailing address changes on a bill, and every homestead, disability or senior freeze exemption: Assessor
  • Complaints about how large the bill is: the taxing districts listed on the bill itself
  • Redeeming delinquent tax: County Clerk, 618-244-8020
  • Making or checking a payment: Treasurer/Collector

Jefferson County housing at a glance

Jefferson County has 36,147 residents, about 2.6 percent fewer than at the 2020 count, and 14,820 households, of which 71.7 percent own their home. The typical owner-occupied house is valued at $126,000, and the median household brings in $63,118. Monthly housing costs for owner households come to $1,278 with a mortgage and $578 without.

With homes in that range, one delinquent bill or a roof repair eats a visible slice of equity. A seller who's behind on tax and wants to skip listing prep can weigh an as-is cash sale against a traditional listing.

Billing and due dates

Real estate tax here is billed one year in arrears, and the Treasurer page posts each year's calendar. The 2025 assessment year is payable in 2026. An installment turns delinquent after the later of June 1 or the date printed on the bill, and then interest of 1 1/2 percent a month, or part of a month, begins. Mail postmarked on the due date still counts as timely.

For 2025 taxes payable in 2026, bills were mailed July 29, the first installment was due August 28 and the second September 28. Delinquent tax was published November 5, and the annual tax sale auction is set for November 20, 2026. These dates move from one cycle to the next, so request the calendar for the year your closing falls in. Mobile home tax runs on its own track with a separate due date.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Jefferson County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Ways to pay

Several routes exist, each with a catch. Make checks out to the Jefferson County Collector.

Jefferson County payment routes
RouteCostCatch
Online, via the QR code on the billE-checks free; cards 2.25% or a $2.00 minimumPaperless billing and autopay available on the county's payment site
Local banksNone listedOnly through the due date, and the stub must come along
U.S. MailNone listedPostmarked no later than the installment date, with the stub
Treasurer's counterNone listedCash, check or money order only; no cards

Send a personal check at least 45 days before the tax sale so it has time to clear. Escrowed? You still have to hand the bill to your lender.

The county also takes optional prepayments for roughly six months after the second installment, up to 100 percent of the last bill, provided no earlier year is delinquent.

The tax sale and mobile homes

Two changes affect anyone carrying unpaid tax. For the 2025 tax payable in 2026 onward, the county used Public Act 104-0553 to take over delinquent real estate taxes itself, holding them for the taxing districts. The county also put the Single Bidder Rule in place effective January 2026. Private buyers still bid on delinquent mobile home taxes.

Foreclosed parcels go to a separate sealed bid auction, and bids can be placed online at iltaxsale.com. Under state law, property sold at a tax sale can generally be redeemed within 3 years of the sale date, with exceptions tied to the property's condition on that date.

Mobile homes have an extra step. Taxes must be paid up to date before the home is moved or sold, and a tax certification from the Treasurer's office, costing $5, is filed with the Illinois Secretary of State to clear the title. Earlier unpaid years must be settled before the county takes current-year payment.

How to challenge your assessment

Complaints are written and addressed to the Board of Review, which the Assessor's office runs. Under state law you get 30 calendar days from publication of the assessment list. Watch the newspaper notice, and ask the Assessor's office what deadline it posted for that year.

The Board of Review has three appointed members. After its written decision, you can petition the Property Tax Appeal Board within 30 days of that notice. Assessments outside Cook County are set at 33 1/3 percent of fair cash value, and the published notice gives a median level you can use to test your own figure.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Jefferson County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Homestead and senior exemptions

These are the common homestead reductions from the Assessor's exemption page, with dollar figures as the county prints them. Each lowers equalized assessed value, not the bill itself.

  • General homestead: any increase over the 1977 value, capped at $6,000, for an owner-occupant
  • Senior citizen homestead: $5,000 once an owner reaches 65
  • Senior assessment freeze: household income of $65,000 or less for the 2025 application, with a new state law raising the limit in later years
  • Homestead improvement: added value to a maximum of $75,000 a year for four years after completion
  • Persons with disabilities: $2,000. Returning veteran: $5,000 for two years.
  • Disabled veteran: $2,500 for a 30 to under 50 percent rating, $5,000 for 50 to under 70 percent, and the first $250,000 of value at 70 percent or above

The senior deferral program behaves like a loan: up to $7,500 of tax a year is deferred at 3 percent simple interest, repayable when the home sells or the owner dies, with applications taken January 1 through March 1. Anyone in this program should get the payoff total from the Treasurer before listing.

Before closing on a Jefferson County sale

Print the parcel record from jeffersonil.devnetwedge.com, the county's inquiry site for bills and payments. Give the title company your parcel number plus the address the county mails to. If you've moved out, send the Assessor a change of address so later bills reach the right person.

Then find out whether an installment is open, whether a deferral lien exists and whether a lender escrows the tax. Have your title company explain how this year's tax gets divided at closing, and say in the contract who covers the bill that comes later. If a bill is already delinquent, get the interest-inclusive total from the Treasurer, and ask the County Clerk about any sold tax.

Frequently asked questions

What dates appear on a Jefferson County tax calendar?

For taxes payable in 2026 the installments were August 28 and September 28. Go by the date on your own bill, and since the calendar changes by year, request the cycle that matches your closing.

Who handles exemptions in Jefferson County?

The Assessor's office, at 618-244-8016. The Treasurer can't help with homestead, disability or senior freeze exemptions or with address changes on bills.

Can I pay Jefferson County tax with a card?

Yes, through the online payment site, where the charge is 2.25% or a $2.00 minimum. E-checks are free, and the courthouse counter accepts no cards.

What happens if Jefferson County tax stays unpaid?

The installment accrues interest after the due date, the parcel is published as delinquent, and the amount goes to the annual tax sale. After a sale, redemption goes through the County Clerk at 618-244-8020.

Must mobile home tax be current before I sell in Jefferson County?

Yes. Mobile home taxes must be paid to date before a move or sale, and a $5 certification goes to the Illinois Secretary of State for a clear title.

Jersey County housing at a glance

Jersey County is a river county north of St. Louis, with Jerseyville as its seat and largest community. It sits inside the St. Louis metro area. Population is 21,160, down 1.7 percent from the 2020 base, across 7,965 households, 80.5 percent of them owner-occupied. The median owner-occupied value is $171,900 and median household income is $80,361. About one resident in four is 65 or older, which matters for tax relief, since the Assessor's office helps seniors prepare the senior homestead exemption and assessment freeze applications.

Most of the county sits in Jersey Community Unit School District 100, with smaller parts in Southwestern District 9, Alton District 11 and Greenfield District 10. Look up your parcel number first, because township, school district and floodplain status all follow the parcel.

Jersey County property tax offices

The Treasurer, the Supervisor of Assessments, the Board of Review and the Code Administrator all work from the Government Building at 200 North Lafayette in Jerseyville, on the same weekday schedule, 8 to 4. The County Clerk answers rate questions and receives redeemed tax.

Jersey County offices a seller may need
OfficeSuite and phoneHandles
TreasurerSuite 5, (618) 498-5571 ext. 109, 110 or 111Billing, collection, delinquent tax
Supervisor of AssessmentsSuite 4, (618) 498-5571 ext. 126Assessments, exemptions, name and address changes
Code AdministratorSuite 6, (618) 498-5571 ext. 145Building and floodplain permits, property maintenance
County Clerk(618) 498-5571, option 6Tax rates, recording, redemption of sold tax

One township assessor serves Jersey, Fidelity and Ruyle townships together, and another serves Mississippi Township. Township assessors get the first look at an assessment, so call yours before you file anything.

Billing and payment

Real estate tax is billed a year behind, while mobile home tax is for the current year. Due dates differ from year to year, so ask the Treasurer's office for the calendar covering your closing date. Interest is charged on anything paid after a due date, at 1 1/2 percent for each month, or fraction of one, in counties of this size.

You have these ways to pay:

  • Online at jerseycountytax.com, where transaction fees apply
  • Any of five Jerseyville banks, up to the due date only: Farmers State Bank, Heartland Bank & Trust, Jersey State Bank, Jerseyville Banking Center and Royal Banks
  • The Treasurer's office or by mail once a bill is delinquent
  • Mobile home tax, which can be paid only at the Treasurer's office or by mail

A few habits save trouble at closing. Pay at a bank only while the bill is current, because banks stop taking it after the due date and the Treasurer's office or the mail becomes the route. Keep the confirmation from any online payment, since transaction fees apply and the receipt shows what year you paid. If you sold midyear, tell the buyer which year's bill is still coming, as real estate tax lags by a year.

A second property tax site, jerseyil.devnetwedge.com, is linked from the county pages for parcel inquiries.

The tax sale

The sale takes place in the auditorium of the Government Building. Only the delinquent taxes are sold, not the property itself, and once taxes are sold they must be redeemed through the County Clerk's office. If taxes stay delinquent for 3 years, the tax buyer can petition the court for a tax deed. The redemption law carries exceptions that depend on the property's status on the sale date.

Before you list, ask the County Clerk for a redemption figure, since sold tax has to be redeemed there.

How to contest an assessment

Begin with your township assessor, who has the first chance to change a value. If you can't agree, ask the Board of Review for a hearing. The Board has three appointed members and hears complaints on value or exempt status for homes, businesses, condominiums and vacant land. It doesn't control the tax dollar amount, and a complaint about the bill itself isn't valid.

A complaint must reach the Board no later than 30 calendar days after the newspaper prints the assessment list, and the county posts a deadline each year. Bring evidence to the hearing:

  • An exterior photo of your property and photos of at least three similar properties in your neighborhood
  • Your property record card and the cards of comparable homes with lower assessments
  • A recent appraisal, sales contract, settlement statement or deed, if you have one

The Board mails its ruling. If you still disagree, the state Property Tax Appeal Board accepts a petition filed within 30 days of the decision notice. The Assessor's forms page carries the Non-Farm Complaint (PTAX-230) and the Farm Complaint (PTAX-227). Miss the window and you wait for the next assessment list.

Exemption forms

The Assessor's documents page lists applications by number, and the office helps seniors prepare theirs. Ask for current dollar limits, because the county page names forms rather than amounts.

  • PTAX-329 and PTAX-340: senior citizens homestead exemption and assessment freeze, with separate 2025 and 2026 versions posted
  • PTAX-343 and PTAX-343R: disabled person's homestead, initial and renewal
  • PTAX-342 and PTAX-342R: standard homestead for disabled veteran
  • PTAX-341: returning veteran
  • PTAX-323: homestead improvement
  • PTAX-245: disaster area reassessment

For a house that was damaged, the disaster form may matter before you sell.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Jersey County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Floodplain and permit rules

These can affect a sale. The Code Administration office reviews plans, issues building, storm water and floodplain permits, inspects new or substantially altered construction, and keeps elevation certificates for unincorporated Jersey County. It also keeps records of substantial improvements or damage to structures in the floodplain and investigates complaints under the International Property Maintenance Code.

Before listing a river-side or low-lying home, ask that office whether the parcel is in a mapped floodplain, whether any permit was left open, and whether a substantial-damage record exists. Manufactured homes fall under a county mobile home ordinance, and the Assessor's housing page links the state installation rules.

Selling with taxes owed

Taxes owed don't block a sale, but they have to be settled with the right office. Here is a workable order:

  • Look up the parcel on the county's online tax site, or call the Treasurer at (618) 498-5571, to see which years are open.
  • If any year was sold, get the redemption figure from the County Clerk.
  • Get a written payoff for the closing date from the Treasurer.
  • Check with the Code Administrator on open permits or floodplain records.

Bring your parcel number to the Government Building if you go in person; one trip to Suites 4 and 5 covers the assessment record and the tax balance. A cash sale skips lender appraisal and repair demands, but the tax payoff and any permit questions still have to be cleared before title can pass.

Frequently asked questions

When is Jersey County property tax due?

Due dates differ from year to year, and real estate tax is billed a year behind. Ask the Treasurer at (618) 498-5571 for the dates tied to your closing.

Where do I pay Jersey County property tax in person?

At any of five Jerseyville banks until the due date. After that, pay at the Treasurer's office in the Government Building at 200 North Lafayette, Suite 5.

Can I appeal my Jersey County assessment after the deadline?

The Board of Review handles complaints during a 30-day window after publication, so a missed window means waiting for the next assessment list.

Does the Board of Review lower my tax bill?

No. It reviews assessed value only. The tax dollar amount isn't a valid complaint, and rate questions go to the County Clerk.

What is the fastest way to find out if my Jersey County parcel has tax sold?

Look the parcel up on the county's online tax site or call the Treasurer. If taxes were sold, redemption is made at the County Clerk's office.

  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Jo Daviess County, IL Property Tax Guide sale

Selling in Jo Daviess County? Get a Cash Offer

Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in Jo Daviess County?
We buy Jo Daviess County houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

Jo Daviess County at a glance

Galena is the seat of Jo Daviess County, the far northwest corner of Illinois. Population is 21,594 and the county holds 13,535 housing units but only 10,391 households. The gap points to many vacation and second homes. Of the occupied homes, 80.4 percent are owned by their residents. The median home value is $209,900 and median household income is $73,993. People 65 and older are 31.5 percent of residents, which means plenty of estate and downsizing listings.

The second-home mix matters at tax time. Homestead relief goes only to full-time resident owners, so an out-of-state buyer cannot count on a seller's exemptions following the house.

Who to call about taxes

The Treasurer and the Assessment Office share the County Courthouse, 330 North Bench Street in Galena. They keep weekday hours of 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. and close for holidays.

Jo Daviess County tax and assessment offices
OfficeLocation and phoneWhat it handles
County TreasurerSuite 149, 815-777-0355Prints and mails bills, collects tax, grants deferrals, runs the annual sale
Assessment OfficeSuite 1B, 815-777-1016Property records, exemptions, equalization, clerk to the Board of Review
Township assessorsListed on the county site by township groupFirst review of a township's values

Each parcel has a property record card at the Assessment Office, which follows ownership through deeds filed with the recorder and mails a notice when an assessment changes. Not sure which township group your address belongs to? Phone them before the sign goes up.

Billing and collection

The Treasurer also serves as County Collector and bills for roughly 110 local taxing bodies. Once bills are mailed, you pay in two installments. Whatever is still unpaid when the year ends goes into the annual tax sale, after the county publishes notice. Late installments pick up interest at 1 1/2 percent per month or part of a month, a rate the state sets for counties of this size (interest section of the Property Tax Code).

Anyone can reprint a bill from the free parcel search on the county site. Online payment runs through Govtech Services, which also lets an owner set up a personal escrow or advance payment. The Treasurer's forms page carries a deferral application, a direct deposit form and tax sale buyer registration forms. It also has hotel and motel use tax returns, so a lodging owner should confirm those are current before selling.

Ask the Treasurer for the installment dates tied to your own bill.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Jo Daviess County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Tax rates

The county's rates span about 6.4554% to 11.21326%, and the median is 8.01228%. Where you land in that spread depends on the school, village, park and other districts your parcel sits in, and and those bodies, not the Assessment Office, set the rate. An exemption trims taxable value before the rate is applied, so what it saves you depends on your parcel's rate. Comparing houses? Look at the taxing districts printed on each bill.

How to appeal your assessment

The Board of Review hears complaints. It has three appointed members and sits no later than the first Monday in June. Your complaint has to be written on the county's form and carry original signatures, because faxes are refused. The statute sets a window of 30 calendar days from publication of the assessment list (complaint section of the Property Tax Code).

Filing windows differ by township and are announced in a local newspaper. Once a window closes, the Board cannot accept a late complaint. Notices run in either The Galena Gazette or The Scoop depending on the township, so ask the Assessment Office which one covers you.

Still unhappy after the Board rules? You can petition the Property Tax Appeal Board within 30 days of the written notice (appeal board section of the Property Tax Code). For reference, assessments outside Cook County are set at 33 1/3 percent of fair cash value (valuation section of the Property Tax Code).

Homestead exemptions and the residency rule

The Assessment Office administers these programs:

  • General homestead and homestead improvement.
  • Senior citizen homestead and senior citizen assessment freeze (PTAX-340).
  • Disabled persons (PTAX-343), disabled veteran (PTAX-342) and returning servicemember (PTAX-341) exemptions.
  • Disabled veteran standard exemption.

You need to live in the county full time. If asked, produce two of these three documents: an Illinois driver's license, a federal tax return or an Illinois voter registration card, each listing the property address. Without two of the three, the homestead exemption is denied. Once bills have been printed, a missing renewal form for the low-income senior freeze, disabled person or disabled veteran exemption costs you that exemption for the year, with no exceptions.

Two other programs fit older homes. Senior Citizen Real Estate Tax Deferral comes through the Treasurer, with applications open after January 1. The Historic Freeze can hold the assessed value of an owner-occupied historic home for eight years, followed by a four-year step-up. It applies only after the state historic preservation office approves the rehabilitation, and the county starts the freeze only once it has that office's certificate.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Jo Daviess County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

What to bring to the office

Prepare before you drive to the courthouse. At the Treasurer's window, have the parcel number or the property address and your most recent bill, plus the lender's name if the tax is escrowed. For the Assessment Office, bring your deed or closing statement, the last assessment notice, and any exemption renewal forms you received in the mail. If you are asking about a deferral, bring the application you picked up after January 1. Staff can usually tell you on the spot whether a parcel sits in a township group with a filing window still open.

Before you close a sale

Run down these items before signing a contract:

  • Pull the parcel from the county's free property search and compare it with your last bill.
  • Confirm which township group assesses the parcel.
  • Find out whether a deferral lien, a historic freeze or an exemption renewal is pending.
  • If a lender escrows your tax, ask it for the year's payment history.
  • Tell the title company about any lodging or short-term rental activity, since hotel and motel returns are filed with the Treasurer.

Spell out in the contract who covers the bill that arrives after closing and how the year is divided. If the house is a parent's estate, pull the exemption and deferral records early. A deferral lien will show up in the buyer's title search and has to be cleared at closing.

A cash sale skips the lender's appraisal and underwriting, which helps when an old house has tax or record questions still open. Even then, the tax bill and any lien are settled from the proceeds at the closing table.

Frequently asked questions

Is Jo Daviess County property tax paid in two parts?

Yes. Real estate tax comes due in two installments once bills are mailed. The exact dates are printed on your bill, and the Treasurer can confirm them.

Can I still file an assessment appeal this year?

Only if your township window is open. The Board of Review cannot take complaints after the filing date, so call the Assessment Office at 815-777-1016 to confirm where your township stands.

What proof of residency does the county require for exemptions?

Two of three documents: an Illinois driver's license, a federal tax return or an Illinois voter registration card, each showing the property address.

Who do I call about my assessment?

Start with the assessor for the township where the home sits, or reach the county Assessment Office at 815-777-1016.

Does the county offer a tax deferral for seniors?

Yes. The Treasurer reviews and grants deferrals, and the application is available from that office after January 1 each year. Call 815-777-0355.

Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in Johnson County?

Johnson County housing at a glance

Vienna anchors Johnson County, a rural stretch of far southern Illinois with about 13,363 residents and roughly 5,555 housing units. Homeownership runs 82.0 percent among 4,101 households. The median owner-occupied value is $160,500 against a median household income of $62,528. Monthly owner costs have a median of $1,510 with a mortgage and $510 without.

Few new houses are going up, so buyers here mostly shop resale homes like yours. Paid tax bills and a clean title speed things along.

Offices and phone numbers

Deed records at the County Clerk and Recorder reach back to 1815, and that office also records mortgages, keeps plat books and tracks delinquent taxes. Phone lines for each office are listed here.

Johnson County tax offices
OfficePhoneWhy a seller calls
Treasurer618-658-8042Bill amounts, payment, delinquent status
Assessor618-658-8010Assessment, exemptions, parcel questions
County Clerk and Recorder618-658-3611Recording a deed, delinquent tax records
Addressing618-658-5911Rural address questions

Find the Clerk at 105 North 6th Street, Vienna, in the courthouse and administration building. Weekday hours are 8 to noon and 1 to 4. You can also arrange an appointment outside those hours.

Searching and paying your bill online

The county runs a property tax inquiry portal at johnsonil.devnetwedge.com. It has separate searches for parcels and mobile homes and a link to pay. Type in a parcel number, an owner name or a street address and print the result for the title company.

Installment dates change each year and appear on the bill, so confirm them with the Treasurer. Illinois sets the lateness rule. Pay the first installment after the later of June 1 or the bill's printed date and it is delinquent, costing 1 1/2 percent for every month or fraction of a month in a county of this size (interest section of the Property Tax Code). A postmark on or before the deadline counts as on time. The second installment works the same way against September 1.

Should the lender that escrows your tax let the bill go delinquent, the interest lands on the lender. Call your servicer first if a bill shows as unpaid.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Johnson County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Assessments and how to contest one

Assessed value outside Cook County is meant to be 33 1/3 percent of fair cash value, measured on January 1 of the general assessment year (valuation section of the Property Tax Code). Counties of this size publish the list in a local paper by December 31. The notice carries the median assessment level, the last day to file and a note on homestead exemptions (publication section of the Property Tax Code).

Here is a quick test. Divide your assessed value by the median level shown in the notice. A result higher than a realistic sale price suggests the house is over-assessed. In that case, file a written complaint with the Board of Review within 30 calendar days of publication. Mailed complaints are judged by postmark (complaint section of the Property Tax Code). A second level exists. After the Board decides, a petition to the Property Tax Appeal Board is due within 30 days of the written notice (appeal board section of the Property Tax Code).

The Assessor at 618-658-8010 can say where the Board of Review accepts complaints and which forms and rules apply.

Homestead exemptions

Amounts come from state law. Because no neighboring county has 3,000,000 or more people, Johnson County gets the lower tier of each exemption from 2023 onward:

  • General homestead: the rise in equalized value above the 1977 figure, up to $6,000 (general homestead section).
  • Senior citizens homestead: up to $5,000, for an owner 65 or older who owes the taxes (senior homestead section).
  • Senior owners may also qualify to defer taxes, and the assessor must tell exemption holders about it.

Here, a homestead exemption lasts through the end of the year the house sells. After that the assessor may require the new owner to apply again, so a buyer should file early.

Disability, returning servicemember and improvement exemptions each have their own state forms. Ask the Assessor which applications are due this cycle and whether any renewal is waiting.

Selling with taxes owed

Tax left unpaid can be auctioned at a tax sale, and delinquent records sit with the Clerk. A buyer's claim from that sale can generally be redeemed within 3 years of the sale date, though some properties follow different rules depending on their status that day (redemption section of the Property Tax Code).

Behind on the bill? Get a payoff with interest from the Treasurer, check with the Clerk for any sold tax on the parcel, and hand both figures to the title company. Settling the balance from proceeds at closing is routine, as long as the contract says so.

A cash buyer does not wait for a lender's approval, which helps if a payoff or title question needs extra days. The tax still comes out of your proceeds.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Johnson County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

How a sale plays out at the courthouse

Few steps are involved. With a buyer lined up, the title company runs a tax search and checks bill status with the Treasurer. Anything owed is paid off at the closing table. Afterward the deed is recorded with the Clerk and Recorder, and the Assessor changes the parcel's owner. Later bills go to the buyer, so put the year's split in writing.

Getting the house ready to list

Begin on the inquiry portal and confirm the parcel's owner name matches your deed.

  • Print the record and your last assessment notice for the buyer.
  • Pay or schedule the current installment, and ask your lender about escrow.
  • If a rural parcel needs a corrected address, call the Addressing line at 618-658-5911.

Is the deed still in a late relative's name? The Clerk and Recorder can explain what to file to record a transfer. A manufactured home on the land needs its own search under the portal's mobile home tab.

Gather a short packet before the first showing: the printed parcel record, your latest bill with proof of payment, the assessment notice, and the exemption paperwork if you hold any. Buyers and their agents ask for these early, and having them ready keeps an offer from stalling over small questions. If you are over 65 and defer taxes, tell the title company up front so the deferred amount is paid off with the rest.

The Treasurer at 618-658-8042 and the Assessor at 618-658-8010 are the two numbers worth saving. The first answers anything about what you owe. The second answers anything about how the house is valued or which exemptions are on file.

Frequently asked questions

What installment dates does Johnson County use?

They change yearly and print on each bill, so call the Treasurer at 618-658-8042. The first installment is late after the later of June 1 or the printed date. The second is judged against September 1.

What interest applies to late tax?

Illinois charges 1 1/2 percent per month or fraction of a month here. A postmark by the deadline keeps mail from being late.

Where do I search tax records online?

Go to johnsonil.devnetwedge.com. Parcels and mobile homes have separate searches, and there is a link to pay.

How big is the general homestead exemption?

The cap is $6,000 of equalized assessed value from 2023 on, and the amount is the increase over the 1977 value up to that limit.

Does the homestead exemption pass to a buyer?

Through the end of the sale year, yes. After that the new owner may have to apply, so a buyer should call the Assessor at 618-658-8010.

Selling in Kane County? Get a Cash Offer

Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in Kane County?

Kane County in brief

Kane County lies west of Chicago. Aurora is its biggest city and Geneva its seat, and Elgin, Batavia and St. Charles are also big names here. About 525,757 people live here in 195,957 housing units, and occupants own 76.0 percent of the homes. A typical owned home is worth $327,000 and median household income is $103,163. Owners with a mortgage report $2,256 in monthly costs, and owners without one report $958.

Many small governments overlap here, so two houses a few miles apart can get very different bills. Elgin, Aurora, Batavia, Geneva, St. Charles, Carpentersville, Sugar Grove, Montgomery and Hampshire each add their own taxing bodies on top of the county. One treasurer mails every bill, yet a Geneva address and a Hampshire address may pay different school districts and municipalities.

Who handles what

Property tax work is split across four offices, most on the Government Center campus in Geneva. Expect weekday phone service, and no answer on county holidays. Foreclosures go through the county sheriff, which matters if a sale is racing a lender.

Kane County property tax offices
OfficeHandlesWhere and phone
Township Assessor (16 townships)Initial valuations, questions about your assessed valueDirectory at assessments.kanecountyil.gov
County Assessment OfficeExemptions, assessment complaints, equalization factors719 Batavia Avenue, Building C, Geneva, (630) 208-3818
County Clerk, Tax ExtensionTax rates, delinquent taxes, redemptions719 Batavia Avenue, Building B, Geneva, (630) 232-5964
County TreasurerCurrent tax bills and collection, forfeitures719 Batavia Avenue, Building A, Geneva, (630) 232-3565

How a house gets assessed

Each January 1, your township assessor estimates what the house would fetch, and 33.33 percent of that estimate becomes the assessed value. Real sales from the three prior years drive the estimate. After that, the county Supervisor of Assessments equalizes the townships against each other. Values can also move between general assessment years when a house is added to, torn down, or hit by fire or flood.

All 16 townships elect their own assessor: Aurora, Batavia, Big Rock, Blackberry, Campton, Dundee, Elgin, Geneva, Hampshire, Kaneville, Plato, Rutland, St. Charles, Sugar Grove, Virgil and Burlington. Valuation happens at the township, not at the county seat.

  • Farmland is valued on agricultural economic value.
  • Preferential assessments exist for subdivision lots, historic residences, open space, low-income housing, veteran and fraternal posts, solar energy and railroads, each with its own conditions.
  • The tax cap law (PTELL) limits most local levy increases to 5 percent or inflation, whichever is less. New construction and voter-approved referenda are exceptions.
Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Kane County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

How to appeal your assessment

Talk to your township assessor first. Still disagree? Put a complaint in writing to the Kane County Board of Review, due 30 days after your township's notice runs in a local paper. Three members sit on the Board. They can raise, lower or leave an assessment alone, and they rule on exemption requests.

Three grounds are accepted. Data errors cover things like a record showing 2,400 square feet when a survey shows 2,200. Valuation means the equalized assessed value tops one third of fair cash value. Equity means comparable homes nearby are assessed lower. Complaining that the tax is too high, or rose from last year, will not work, and the Property Tax Appeal Board has said so.

Each township has its own deadline, posted on the county's Assessment Complaints page with residential, commercial and association forms and an electronic evidence portal. Once the tax bill is in your mailbox, that year's chance is gone unless a complaint is already with the Board. The assessment office's email notice warns you when your township publishes.

Homestead and other exemptions

Nine programs are on offer. Most trim taxable value, not the bill. Get applications from the assessment office website or at (630) 208-3818.

  • General Homestead Exemption, up to $8,000, for an owner-occupied principal dwelling, usually without yearly reapplication.
  • Senior Citizen Homestead Exemption, up to $8,000, once an owner turns 65 by the end of the assessment year.
  • Homestead Improvement Exemption, up to $25,000, on a new addition or finished basement for four years.
  • Low-Income Senior Citizen Assessment Freeze, with a yearly application and a household income limit of $65,000.
  • Returning Veteran's Exemption of $5,000 for two years after return from an armed conflict.
  • Disabled veteran standard exemption, up to $250,000, for a service-connected rating of at least 30 percent.
  • Disabled veteran exemption, up to $100,000, for Specially Adapted Housing.
  • Persons with Disabilities Exemption of $2,000.
  • Natural Disaster Exemption for reconstruction after a disaster.

Senior Services of Aurora and Senior Services of Elgin also help seniors apply.

Due dates and penalties

Taxes come due in two parts, June 1 and September 1, with bills in the mail by May 1. Miss a due date and interest of 1 1/2 percent per month or fraction of a month starts, as set for counties this size by 35 ILCS 200/21-15. Taxes still unpaid can go to the annual tax sale. After a sale, a principal dwelling can be redeemed for two and one half years and other property for two years, with interest and costs added to the tax. Redemption is handled by the County Clerk's Tax Extension office, not the treasurer.

Ways to pay include online e-check (free), a drive-up drop box behind Building A, participating Kane County banks with a payment coupon, mail, the treasurer's counter, and the Clerk's Aurora and Elgin branch offices for personal checks or money orders. A bill reprint is free online or $2.00 at the counter.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Kane County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Who pays when a house sells

Because the tax follows the property, a buyer may get a bill covering a year you lived there. New owners are advised to check the closing statement for a seller credit or ask their attorney.

The bill due in a given year covers the prior tax year, so a sale can fall between a paid installment and an unpaid one. Your closing agent can show how the settlement statement splits the bill. The Treasurer can report payment status for your parcel number (PIN), and the Clerk can estimate redemption if a prior year went unpaid. The PIN is printed on the bill and on the assessment notice, and the Property Search tool on the assessment site finds it by address.

If taxes are owed, get the payoff from the treasurer, settle it from your proceeds at closing, and have the title company confirm nothing was sold. A cash sale skips a lender's underwriting, so these checks are often the only thing left that can slow a closing.

Where the money goes

Schools take the largest share. The rest is split among municipalities, the county and other local governments. Each taxing body sets its own levy, and the county issues a levy only for itself.

Residential property supplies 75.7 percent of the tax base, commercial 12.8 percent, industrial 9.6 percent and farm 1.7 percent. Rates run generally between about 6 and 9 percent, with a median near 7.5 percent. A parcel lookup on the county's tax data site shows how much of one property's bill goes to each district.

Frequently asked questions

Which Kane County office sends the bill?

The Treasurer collects current taxes from Building A of the Government Center in Geneva, (630) 232-3565. For rates or redemption, call the Clerk's Tax Extension office at (630) 232-5964.

How long do owners have to file a complaint?

Thirty days, counted from the newspaper publication of your township's notice. The Board of Review takes the complaint, and publication dates differ by township.

What happens if I do not pay?

Interest runs at 1 1/2 percent a month, and the taxes can be sold at the annual tax sale. A principal dwelling keeps a two and one half year redemption period.

Can I sell with taxes owing?

Yes, but the unpaid amount must be settled at closing or credited to the buyer, because the tax stays with the property. Ask the treasurer for the payoff and the clerk for a redemption estimate if taxes were sold.

Is there a senior exemption?

Yes. There is a senior exemption of up to $8,000 and a separate assessment freeze that depends on household income.
