What happens if taxes go unpaid

After each due date, a penalty of one and a half percent accrues every month, and it is not prorated. Section 21-15 of the Property Tax Code uses that rate for counties below 3,000,000 people.

In October, certified letters go to owners of unpaid parcels, and a notice runs in the Village Voices. The unpaid taxes are offered at a November tax sale. The sale auctions the tax, not the house, and a buyer who wins takes a lien at the interest rate bid. Afterward the delinquent records move to the County Clerk, 815-235-8289, who quotes redemption amounts.

A home is at risk only if nothing clears the lien in 30 months. For certificates issued since the start of 2024, 35 ILCS 200/21-350 allows redemption for 3 years after the sale in most cases, so ask the clerk which period covers your parcel.

Taxes when a Stephenson County house sells

A split between buyer and seller is usually settled at closing and set out in the contract. Until a bill is paid, the present owner answers for the whole amount. A parcel with a balance can still change hands, since the unpaid tax is deducted from what the seller receives.

Before you list, take these steps:

  • Print the parcel's history from the county portal, which goes back to the 2000 tax year for most parcels.
  • Call the treasurer for the exact penalty on a late installment. The schedule is also printed on each coupon.
  • Check with your mortgage company whether it pays from escrow. If it does, a lender at fault for a late payment bears the penalty.
  • Confirm with the Assessor that exemptions on the parcel are current.

A Stephenson County house in rough shape can sell as is for cash, with the tax due paid at the table.

Frequently asked questions

When is the last day to pay before the Stephenson County tax sale?

Early November, with the two halves due in late June and early September. A penalty of one and a half percent a month follows each due date.

Which office decides how much my Stephenson County bill is?

None alone. Assessors set values, taxing bodies set levies, and the county clerk extends rates. The Treasurer collects and cannot alter values, exemptions or amounts.

Does Stephenson County take a partial payment on an installment?

No. The two equal installments fall in June and September, and Illinois law bars the collector from accepting less than a full installment. A partial check is mailed back.

Is the county assessor responsible for Freeport parcels?

No. Freeport Township assesses its own parcels, which carry numbers starting with 18, while the county office covers the other 17 townships. Call the township office at 815-232-6131.

What is the deadline for a Stephenson County assessment complaint?

Thirty calendar days after your township's change list is published. The Board of Review cannot take a late complaint, and the state appeal needs a board decision first.

Tazewell County tax offices in Pekin

Tazewell County keeps its tax offices together in the McKenzie Building at 11 South Fourth Street in Pekin, ZIP 61554. The Treasurer and Collector is in Suite 308 at 309-477-2284. The Assessment Office and the Board of Review share Suite 410, at 309-477-2275 and 309-477-2277. The treasurer and the board both open at 8 on weekday mornings and close at 4:30.

Each office answers a different question:

  • Treasurer: where to pay, what is owed, tax sale information.
  • Assessment Office: homestead exemption forms, senior freeze renewals, name and address changes, and township assessor contacts.
  • Board of Review: written appeals of an assessed value.

File a first homestead exemption in person so staff can check the information. The senior freeze mailing reflects a higher income limit of $75,000.

Housing in Tazewell County

Pekin, on the Illinois River, is the biggest city in Tazewell County, which belongs to the Peoria metro area. Most residents live along the western edge. The county spans 658 square miles and has an estimated 130,049 people, down slightly from 131,343 at the 2020 count. Its 58,550 housing units include 7.8 percent sitting vacant, and owners live in about three of every four occupied homes (75.7 percent).

School districts shape buyer interest here. Pekin Community High School District 303, Washington District 308 and East Peoria District 309 are the secondary districts, while Morton Community Unit District 709, Eureka Unit District 140 and Tremont District 702 are among the K-12 districts. Name the district in your listing, since buyers search by it.

Installment dates and interest

The first half of each bill is due June 1 and the second half September 1. Payments must be received by those dates or interest runs at 1-1/2 percent a month. A bill that arrives late, or never, gives the owner no relief from that interest.

Usual Tazewell County collection calendar
StepUsual date
First installment dueJune 1
Second installment dueSeptember 1
Tax sale of unpaid taxesOctober

The treasurer disburses what it collects to the units of government on each bill. The detailed payment notes are printed on the back of the bill, and written questions to the office are answered by return mail.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Tazewell County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Ways to pay

The treasurer takes payments at the counter, by mail and electronically. Checks go to Tazewell County Treasurer, 11 S. Fourth St., Suite 308, Pekin, IL 61554. Electronic payments run by phone at 1-309-925-0025 or online with American Express, MasterCard, Discover, Visa, debit cards, PayPal or e-check.

  • Cards and debit cards add a convenience fee of 2.25 percent of the taxes, never below $1.95 per transaction.
  • E-checks carry a flat $1.25 fee.
  • The provider keeps the fee. None of it goes to Tazewell County.
  • You need the 12-digit parcel number from the top right corner of the bill.

If you cannot find the number, call 309-477-2284 for help. The same fees apply to card payments made at the counter.

How does a Tazewell County owner appeal an assessed value?

Start with the township or county assessor, because a mistake caught early may be fixed without a formal appeal. If that fails, file a written complaint with the Board of Review. The state rule (35 ILCS 200/16-55) allows 30 calendar days from publication of the assessment list, and the Board posts the exact filing deadline each year.

Three members make up the Board of Review, named by the County Board, and its session opens on the first Monday of June and ends December 31. It deals only with assessed valuations before equalization, not the tax rate or the bill. A formal appeal needs one of four grounds:

  • The assessor's market value is higher than actual market value, shown by a recent open-market purchase or an appraisal.
  • The assessment is a higher share of market value than the township or county median level in a sales ratio study.
  • The assessment rests on wrong facts, such as a mismeasured lot or building.
  • Similar neighboring properties are assessed lower.

Helpful evidence: the property record card, photos, comparable sales, an appraisal, and Form PTAX-203 from a recent purchase. Once the bill arrives, it is generally too late to contest that year's assessment. A ruling you dispute can be taken to the state appeals board or to circuit court.

Exemptions, forms and equalization

The Assessment Office posts forms for several exemptions and relief programs. The list covers Disabled Persons (form 343, with a physician's statement on 343A), Disabled Veteran (342), Returning Veteran (341) and Solar Assessment (330). Annual renewal forms and a Disaster Proclamation form (245) are posted as well.

Owners can also request a name or address change, a split or a combination of parcels. Fraternal and veteran organizations have freeze forms of their own.

Equalization is one uniform percentage raise or cut applied to an area or class of property so that assessments average 33.33 percent of market value. Local assessment officials and the state revenue department both do this work. Township assessors hold the local detail, and the county page links to a directory of them.

What happens if Tazewell County taxes are not paid?

Taxes still unpaid go to registered tax buyers at the yearly sale, held in October. The buyer adds interest and penalty, and the treasurer's page carries buyer registration forms and sale results.

The sale transfers a lien. It does not transfer the house. The owner may redeem for 3 years after the sale when the certificate was issued from 2024 forward, with some exceptions such as vacant property. Late-installment interest comes from 35 ILCS 200/21-15, which sets 1 1/2 percent a month or part of a month for a county this size.

The same section puts the interest on a lender that holds enough escrow money and still pays late. Owners who are behind should confirm the payoff and the sale status of the parcel with the treasurer before agreeing to a closing date.

Taxes before closing

Illinois taxes are paid in arrears, so the bill that comes due in a sale year covers the year before. The purchase contract sets how buyer and seller share it, and the title company carries that out at the table.

  1. Look up the bill with the parcel number and confirm which installments the county shows as paid.
  2. If any installment is late, get the treasurer's payoff figure from Suite 308.
  3. Ask the Assessment Office to remove your homestead or senior exemptions once you no longer live in the house.
  4. Give the title company the correct tax bill address so later bills reach the buyer.

A Tazewell County house needing work can go to a cash buyer as is, with unpaid tax cleared at closing. A cash sale skips the lender's appraisal and any repair demands that come with it, so the date depends mostly on how fast the title company can clear the parcel.

Frequently asked questions

Which dates apply to Tazewell County tax payments?

June 1 for the first half and September 1 for the second. Interest of 1-1/2 percent a month follows each date, and a late-arriving bill is no excuse.

Can I pay Tazewell County taxes with a credit card?

Yes. Cards and debit cards are accepted online, by phone at 1-309-925-0025 and at the counter. The provider charges 2.25 percent with a $1.95 minimum, and e-checks cost a flat $1.25.

How long do I have to appeal a Tazewell County assessment?

Thirty calendar days after the assessment list is published. The Board of Review posts the exact deadline each year, so call 309-477-2277 early.

Can the Board of Review change my rate?

No. The board looks only at the assessed valuation before equalization. Rates and totals come from the taxing districts and sit outside an appeal.

Where do I ask about homestead exemptions in Tazewell County?

Ask the Assessment Office at 309-477-2275 in the McKenzie Building, Suite 410. It posts the exemption forms, and it recommends filing a first homestead exemption in person.

Which Vermilion County office answers which tax question?

The Vermilion County housing market

Vermilion County runs along the Indiana line between the state border and Champaign County, covering 901 square miles. Danville is both the county seat and its biggest city. Population is estimated at 71,259, down from 74,188 at the 2020 count. Of 34,407 housing units, 11.2 percent stand vacant, and owners occupy 67.8 percent of the homes that are lived in.

Interstate 74 passes along Danville's southern edge, with U.S. 136, U.S. 150 and Illinois Route 1 meeting downtown. Four rail lines cross the Danville area, so crossings near a house can matter to a buyer.

Payment dates and cutoffs

The first installment comes due in June and the second in early September, which is also the date for mobile home taxes. The Treasurer then sets a run of cutoffs ahead of the fall sale and posts the exact dates each year.

Final day for any payment, then the property tax saleEarly November

Checks are made payable to Vermilion County Treasurer, and the phone payment line is 1 (877) 221-8591. Owners who want electronic bills can register at vermilion.mcgedoc.com using the code printed on their current statement.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Vermilion County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

How to contest a Vermilion County assessment

A complaint is due at the Board of Review 30 calendar days after the township assessor and Supervisor of Assessments publish their changes, tracking 35 ILCS 200/16-55. The board's rules supply the practical steps.

  • File on the board's approved form, in duplicate, with a complete copy of every document you want considered.
  • Use a separate form for each tract number. The form covers residential, commercial and industrial property, and farmland has its own form.
  • File in person, email brdreview@vercounty.org, or mail it to 201 North Vermilion St, 3rd Floor, Danville, IL 61832.
  • Ownership on January 1 of the assessment year is required.

A complaint touches only the assessment year it is filed for, and that assessment drives the bill payable the following year. The bill in your mailbox now rests on the prior year's assessment. Tax rates are outside the board's power, and it will not hear complaints about them.

What happens after a complaint is filed?

The board reviews the complaint and the attached papers, may look at the property, and mails a Notice of Proposed Decision. An owner who disagrees must request a hearing in writing, on the board's form, within 10 days of the notice date.

A hearing notice follows at least 10 days ahead of the date, and a no-show means dismissal. The board recommends an attorney when the reduction sought is $100,000 or more on a parcel or a combination of parcels.

Any appraisal must meet the Real Estate Appraiser Licensing Act and USPAP, state whether the appraiser holds an Illinois credential, and list the board and Vermilion County as intended users when it supports a complaint. The board will not issue a certificate of error for a mere error of judgment in valuation. After the board rules, a petition to the state Property Tax Appeal Board is possible within 30 days of the written decision notice (35 ILCS 200/16-160).

How the Supervisor of Assessments organizes values

The Supervisor of Assessments office was created by state law to give statistical and performance data to the Illinois Department of Revenue and technical advice to the township assessors and the Board of Review. It keeps the name and address records, assessed values and exemptions, equalizes assessments, and acts as clerk of the Board of Review. It publishes the assessment change notices and mails them to taxpayers.

Vermilion County posts a quadrennial assessment roll covering 19 townships: Blount, Butler, Carroll, Catlin, Danville, Elwood, Georgetown, Grant, Jamaica, Love, McKendree, Middlefork, Newell, Oakwood, Pilot, Ross, Sidell, South Ross and Vance. A parcel's township determines which assessor owns the first look at its value, so find your township on the bill before you call.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Vermilion County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Tax relief for owners

The Treasurer's office points owners to two programs. The first is the Senior Citizens and Disabled Persons Property Tax Relief and Pharmaceutical Assistance Act, with applications from the Illinois Department of Revenue at 800-624-2459. The second is the Senior Citizen Tax Deferral program, and its applications are available in the Treasurer's office at 217-554-6080.

Exemptions that lower the assessed value, such as the homestead exemptions, go through the Supervisor of Assessments instead. The county also posts an application for a general homestead exemption on single-family dwellings subject to a lease.

Unpaid taxes and selling a house that owes

An installment unpaid after its due date is delinquent and accrues interest of 1 1/2 percent a month or part of one, the rate 35 ILCS 200/21-15 sets for counties below 3,000,000 people. Later in the fall the county publishes names of unpaid owners and holds a sale of the taxes, usually in early November.

Whoever buys at the sale gets a tax lien, and the owner keeps a right to redeem. For certificates issued from 2024 forward, 35 ILCS 200/21-350 allows 3 years after the sale, with exceptions. Delinquent-tax questions go to the County Clerk at 217-554-1903, ideally before a closing.

  1. Ask the Treasurer at 217-554-6080 for the amount due on the parcel, with interest.
  2. Ask the County Clerk whether any year has already been sold.
  3. Give the title company both figures so the payoff comes out of your proceeds.
  4. Ask the Supervisor of Assessments to update your name and address records after the deed is recorded.

A Vermilion County house with taxes owed can still go to a cash buyer as is, and the balance is cleared at closing.

Frequently asked questions

When are Vermilion County property taxes due?

The first installment is due in June, and the second installment and mobile home taxes in early September. The Treasurer posts the exact dates each year, along with the cutoffs before the fall sale.

What is the filing window for a Vermilion County assessment complaint?

Thirty calendar days from publication of your township's assessment changes. File two copies on the board's form with supporting documents attached.

Can the Vermilion County board adjust my tax rate?

No. Rates are beyond the board's authority, and it turns away rate complaints. Only the assessed value of the property is reviewable.

Which Vermilion County office has delinquent tax records?

The County Clerk, at 217-554-1903. For bills and payments, the Treasurer's line is 217-554-6080.

Is there a deferral program for seniors in Vermilion County?

Yes. The Treasurer lists a Senior Citizen Tax Deferral program, and applications are available at that office. The Illinois Department of Revenue also supplies applications for the Senior Citizens and Disabled Persons relief act.

Washington County tax offices

Washington County lies in the southern stretch of Illinois and covers roughly 564 square miles around Nashville. Two courthouse offices at 101 E. St. Louis Street do most of the tax work:

  • The Treasurer and Collector prints the bills, receives payments and conducts the delinquent sale. The line is (618) 327-4800, extension 315, open weekdays 8:00 to 4:00.
  • The Supervisor of Assessments keeps valuation records and supports the Board of Review. Dial the same number and ask for extension 166.
  • The County Clerk and Recorder puts the deed on file after a house is sold.

Six school districts overlap the county: Oakdale CCSD 1, West Washington County CUD 10, Irvington CCSD 11, Ashley CCSD 15, Nashville CCSD 49 and Nashville Community High School District 99. The district drawn around a parcel shapes its total tax, so read the bill line by line before quoting a figure to a buyer.

Housing costs in Washington County

Few households here rent. About 84.1% of occupied homes are held by their owners, with a midpoint home value of $155,700.

Washington County housing and income (2020-2024 estimates unless noted)

Interstate 64 and US 51 cross the county, along with Illinois routes 4, 13, 15 and 127, so Nashville sits within reach of the St. Louis side of the river. With just 15 permits issued in 2025, a seller's house competes mostly with other resale listings rather than new builds. Confirm insurance and repair history for any house you list.

The tax calendar

Each year brings two payment dates, and the schedule is reset annually. Bills for the prior year's taxes mail in the summer, with the first half due in September and the second half in October. The Treasurer will confirm the exact Friday dates on your own bill.

The Treasurer enforces those dates and honors the postmark on a mailed check. Not receiving a bill does not excuse a late payment. If yours never arrived, ask the office for a duplicate or print one from the parcel lookup.

Mobile homes follow a separate schedule. Notices go out in April and payment is due June 30. A delinquent notice adds $25.00 per month, with a ceiling of $100.00, and a lien is filed on the unit when the year ends. Online payment is not offered for them.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Washington County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Where can a Washington County bill be paid?

Options include the mail, the online lookup, the counter and the courthouse drop box at the south entrance. Cash never belongs in the box or in the mail.

  • Make checks out to the Washington County Treasurer, 101 E. St. Louis Street, Nashville, IL 62263.
  • Send stub 1 for the first half, stub 2 for the second, or both stubs to settle the year in one payment.
  • Part-payments are refused, and a check that fails to clear voids the payment.
  • To get a receipt back, enclose a return envelope with postage.

Late in the year the Treasurer sets a final day for online payment and personal or business checks, in December. After that date only cash, cashier's checks and money orders are accepted, so pay early if you are close to the sale.

What happens to a late bill

A late installment begins accruing interest at 1 1/2% each month, and the stubs print the new totals. The state code sets the same rate for smaller counties (section 21-15 of the Property Tax Code).

Whatever stays open eventually lands in the delinquent sale, which falls in January. The winning bidder holds a lien rather than the house, and the owner can still redeem. Section 21-350 allows redemption until three years after the sale, subject to listed exceptions, so ask the Treasurer which rule fits the parcel.

Interest keeps adding while a contract sits unsigned. Request a payoff figure before choosing a closing date.

How do you contest a Washington County valuation?

Complaints reach the Board of Review in writing, within thirty days of the date the assessment list is published. Mail is treated as filed on the postmark date (Property Tax Code section 16-55).

The assessment office also serves as the Board's clerk. Call (618) 327-4800, extension 166, to learn when your township's list comes out, and call early because the window is short.

Evidence beats opinion here. Show what similar houses nearby sold for, include a recent appraisal if one exists, and photograph defects that pull value down. The goal is a lower assessed value on your parcel.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Washington County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Homestead exemptions

Washington County is far smaller than a county with 3,000,000 residents, so the smaller statewide caps apply.

  • General homestead: up to $6,000 knocked off the equalized assessed value of a home its owner lives in (section 15-175).
  • Senior exemption: up to $5,000 for an owner who has turned 65 (section 15-170).
  • Low-income senior freeze: pegs the assessed value to a base year for qualifying older owners (section 15-172). The assessment office can give you the income cap and sign-up period.

A sale does not erase the benefit mid-year. It carries through that assessment year, and the assessor may ask the buyer to apply for the next one.

How should a Washington County owner sell a house that owes tax?

Call the Treasurer first and ask for the full amount due on the parcel, penalty included. Also ask whether any year is already headed for the January sale.

  • Copy the parcel number from the bill so the lookup returns the right record.
  • Plan to pay any open half from the proceeds, with the closing agent confirming the payoff figure in writing.
  • See whether a homestead or senior break appears on the bill, and tell the buyer it may have to be requested again.
  • After closing, the new deed goes to the County Clerk and Recorder for filing.

Estates and rentals take longer. The person signing the deed has to be the recorded owner, and delinquent tax can stall the title company, so sort out ownership and the balance first.

On closing day the title company pays off the open tax from your proceeds, then sends the deed to the County Clerk and Recorder. A cash buyer skips the lender's appraisal, so a clean tax record is often the only thing that sets the closing date.

Frequently asked questions

When are Washington County tax payments due?

Two payment dates apply each year and they shift. They have recently fallen in September and October. The Treasurer at (618) 327-4800, extension 315, can confirm the dates on your own bill.

What does a late payment cost in Washington County?

Interest of 1 1/2% per month applies after a due date, with amounts printed on the stubs. The Property Tax Code uses that rate for smaller counties.

Can I pay a Washington County bill online?

Real estate tax can be paid through the parcel lookup the Treasurer links, and the office can tell you which payment types the portal accepts. Mobile home tax has no online option.

What is the cutoff for contesting a Washington County assessment?

Thirty calendar days from publication of the assessment list. File in writing with the Board of Review, and call extension 166 for the form and your township's schedule.

Can a house with back taxes still sell in Washington County?

Yes, as long as the balance is settled at or before closing, since it stays with the parcel. Get a payoff from the Treasurer, pay from the proceeds, and record the deed to the buyer.

Whiteside County at a glance

Whiteside County stretches across 697 square miles of northwestern Illinois, and the Mississippi River marks its western edge. Morrison holds the courthouse, while Sterling is the biggest city. Rock Falls, Fulton and Prophetstown are the other cities, and the villages include Albany, Erie, Lyndon and Tampico.

Your total depends on the parcel's township, one of 22, and on every district layered over it. A city lot and a township-road farmhouse can carry quite different totals at the same assessed value. Buyers may also arrive from across the river in Iowa, so expect them to compare tax bills.

Housing figures

Whiteside County values run lower than most of Illinois. The midpoint owner-occupied home was valued at $127,100 across 2020 to 2024, and 76.9% of homes are occupied by their owners.

The 2020 census tallied 55,691 residents, down from 58,498 a decade earlier, and 8.9% of housing units stood vacant that year. Price against nearby sales, since a falling population keeps buyers choosy.

Who bills and who assesses

The County Collector sends a single bill for each parcel and then splits the money among more than 140 taxing districts.

  • Collector and Treasurer: 200 East Knox Street in Morrison, phone 815-772-5196, weekday hours 8:30 to 4:30.
  • Supervisor of Assessments: sets assessments, handles exemptions and takes address changes. Look up the office and its phone on the county website.
  • The Collector has no say over your valuation, the bill's size, exemptions or your mailing address.

A bill arrives even when your lender pays from escrow, and the county keeps no mortgage records, so direct escrow questions to the lender. For a new mailing address, send the county's change-of-address form to the Supervisor of Assessments.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Whiteside County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

The Whiteside County tax calendar

The year splits into a June installment and a September installment. Bills mail in mid-May, the installments come due in mid-June and at the start of September, and penalties start the next day each time. The mobile home due date is June 1, and the annual tax sale follows in early November.

The sequence works that way because local taxing districts begin their fiscal years on different dates: municipalities on May 1, school districts on July 1 and counties on December 1. Each body adopts a levy ordinance, the County Clerk calculates rates and extends the bill for every taxpayer, and the Treasurer prepares the roll. Past-due accounts pass to the State's Attorney and County Treasurer, and tax buyers file for judgment and run the sale.

Part-payments are refused. Send a whole installment as printed, or the full year by the first date, with the tax stub attached so the check is not returned.

How to pay the Whiteside County Collector

Several channels are open, and each carries its own cutoff.

  • Over the counter at the Treasurer's office in the courthouse during its regular hours.
  • Through the mail, where a postmark dated by the deadline avoids penalty. The county takes no responsibility for lost mail.
  • Automatic ACH debit on every due date, canceled only by a written request.
  • Credit card with a 2.25% surcharge, or e-check with a flat $1.50.
  • At banks on the participating list, bill in hand, up to a cutoff on the September due date.
  • In the drop box just inside the Morrison courthouse's Law Enforcement Center entrance, before 4:30 on the due date.

Write checks to the Whiteside County Collector. A returned check adds $25.00 on top of penalties, and personal checks are not taken in the month before the tax sale.

How homes are assessed and how to appeal

Illinois values property at one-third of market value, or 33.3%. A bill is the final equalized assessed value, less exemptions, multiplied by the rate. An equalization factor evens out the 22 townships, and valuations rest on the prior three years of sales as of January 1, which explains why a bill can rise even when prices dip.

To challenge a figure, set it beside an appraisal or beside recent sales of comparable houses, then raise it with the Supervisor of Assessments office. A formal appeal goes to the Board of Review in writing, inside thirty days after the township publishes, which tracks section 16-55 of the Property Tax Code.

Additions raise value. The office gets copies of building permits and inspects the work in the field. A home improvement exemption softens the increase for four years, up to $25,000 of assessed value, and appears as an adjustment on the bill.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Whiteside County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Which exemptions can homeowners claim?

Whiteside is far from Cook County, so the standard dollar caps apply.

  • General homestead: a reduction of up to $6,000 in equalized assessed value on an owner's residence (section 15-175).
  • Senior citizens: up to $5,000 more, once an owner reaches 65 (section 15-170).
  • Low-income senior freeze: ties a qualifying older owner's assessment to a base year (section 15-172).

If an exemption is missing, ask the Supervisor of Assessments to review the parcel. After a sale the break lasts to the end of that assessment year, and the buyer may need to apply for the next.

Selling with back taxes

Late installments bear interest of 1 1/2% per month or part of one (section 21-15). A postmark by the due date keeps a mailed payment on time.

Open taxes can be sold at the annual sale. The owner may then redeem for up to three years, with exceptions in section 21-350.

  • Ask the Collector for the exact balance, penalty included, ahead of signing a contract.
  • Let the closing agent wire the payoff from your proceeds.
  • A parcel already sold at a tax sale needs a redemption quote and a deadline from the county.

Search by parcel number, not by name. A stale mailing address or an inherited house is where a balance tends to hide.

A cash sale does not change what you owe, but it keeps the timeline short. The buyer's title company finds the balance, subtracts it from your proceeds and records the deed, so you walk away with the tax settled and no follow-up bill.

Before you list, gather the latest tax bill, your parcel number, proof of any exemption you hold and a payoff statement from your lender. Having these in one folder lets a buyer make a firm offer quickly.

Frequently asked questions

What are the Whiteside County tax due dates?

June and September, each with its own date, in mid-June and at the start of September in recent years. The Collector's page carries the calendar for whichever cycle is current.

Can I use a credit card in Whiteside County?

Yes, with a surcharge. Paying by check, in person or by ACH debit skips the surcharge entirely.

Does Whiteside County accept a partial payment?

No. An installment is accepted only in the printed amount, and both may be combined in one payment by the first due date.

How do I challenge a Whiteside County valuation?

Put the complaint in writing and deliver it to the Board of Review inside thirty days after your township publishes. Gather an appraisal or comparable sales beforehand, and bring questions to the assessor's office.

What if I sell a Whiteside County house owing tax?

Call the Collector at 815-772-5196 for a payoff and settle it from the proceeds. Interest keeps adding monthly until the balance clears, so closing is the natural time to pay.

Who handles a Will County property tax bill

Will County is one of the five collar counties around Chicago, with Joliet as its seat and biggest city. Four offices shape a bill. The Treasurer and the Board of Review both operate from the Will County Office Building, 302 N. Chicago Street, Joliet.

  • The Treasurer receives payments, conducts the yearly tax sale and sends the bills.
  • The Supervisor of Assessments coordinates with the township assessors who set values.
  • The Board of Review, second floor, rules on complaints about assessments.
  • The County Clerk accepts redemption money once a sale has happened.

The cities are Joliet, Aurora, Naperville, Lockport, Crest Hill, Braidwood and Wilmington. Villages run from Bolingbrook, Plainfield and Romeoville to Frankfort, Mokena, New Lenox and Peotone. Several straddle county lines, so find out which county actually bills the parcel.

Home costs in Will County

Across 2020 to 2024 the typical Will County home was valued at $319,600. Owners live in 82.8% of homes, and household income at the midpoint is $109,984. The county has an estimated 712,253 people and 259,218 housing units.

The average commute takes 31.4 minutes. Four Metra lines link the county to the Chicago Loop, Amtrak stops at Joliet, and interstates 55, 57, 80 and 355 all pass through, which helps a listing in towns near a station.

When a Will County installment turns delinquent

Section 21-15 of the Property Tax Code treats the first installment as late once the later of June 1 or the day after the printed date arrives, and applies September 1 the same way to the second. Because Will has under 3,000,000 residents, the interest is 1.5% per month or part of a month.

The same section keeps a mailed check on time if it carries a postmark by the due date. It also shifts interest to a mortgage lender that held enough escrow and still let the bill lapse. Confirm with your servicer that a bill was actually paid.

The Treasurer runs a free e-notice program for paperless bills. Enroll at enoticesonline.com using the authorization code printed on your newest bill, after which the paper copy stops. Owners who lost the code can get a new one from the Treasurer's office.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Will County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Where and how to pay Will County taxes

Beyond the online portal, several routes are open, and paying by check carries no charge.

  • Mail a check to 302 N. Chicago St., Joliet, IL 60432, made out to the Will County Treasurer, with a return envelope if you want a receipt.
  • Walk into any of the 100-plus bank branches enrolled in the county program.
  • Call 815-680-2953. Drawing from a checking or savings account is free, and other payment types add convenience fees.
  • Visit the Treasurer's office, which takes cash, checks and cards. Subsequent taxes are accepted there only, weekdays from 8:30 until 3:30, with no exceptions.
  • Use the secure drop box at the Will County Building when the office is closed.

How a Will County assessment complaint works

The Board of Review opens its complaint period every August, and state law frames the deadline as 30 calendar days after publication of the list. Ask your township assessor about any change in value before you file.

Every parcel needs its own complaint unless the parcels are contiguous and share a land use. The form must carry the parcel number, the address, a signature, the owner's mailing address and a daytime phone number. The Board's office, at 302 N. Chicago Street on the second floor, answers at (815) 740-4707.

Hearings come with house rules. Check the Board's portal 48 hours ahead to see whether yours is live, allow 15 minutes for the building's security screening, and know that a late arrival cannot be rescheduled. The Board decides on evidence using the cost, market and income approaches, so bring sales of comparable homes or an appraisal.

Exemptions

Cook County touches Will County, which lifts the dollar caps above the statewide minimums.

  • General homestead: up to $8,000 off equalized assessed value for a county next to one of 3,000,000 or more (section 15-175).
  • Senior citizens: up to $8,000 once an owner is 65, under the same adjacency rule (section 15-170).
  • Low-income senior freeze (section 15-172), which has its own income test.

The county's property tax pages carry a section for exemptions and deferrals, and the Senior Citizens Real Estate Tax Deferral Act offers older owners a separate route. After a sale, the exemption holds through that assessment year, and the new owner may have to apply.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Will County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

The Will County tax sale and redemption

Delinquent taxes put a lien on the property and are sold to investors, called tax buyers, at an annual sale. Bidders name the interest rate they will accept, and the lowest rate wins. What changes hands is a claim on the tax debt, and the home stays with the owner.

Owners typically get one to three years after the sale to redeem before a buyer may begin court action, while section 21-350 sets three years with exceptions. The County Clerk's tax redemption department collects redemption payments, usually beginning one to two weeks after the sale.

The Treasurer's annual tax sales page links information for property owners and instructions for subsequent taxes. Read it before listing a house that has fallen behind.

What should a Will County seller do about taxes at closing?

Request a payoff from the Treasurer and have the title company confirm each open tax year. If a year was sold, redemption runs through the County Clerk, so the title agent should look for that too.

  • Take the parcel number from the bill and note the township.
  • See whether a homestead or senior exemption is on the bill and let the buyer know.
  • Clear open installments, plus the 1.5% monthly interest, from the proceeds.
  • Record the deed with the Recorder of Deeds, whose fees and transfer tax rules appear on the county recorder page.

Inherited houses and rentals add title work, and back tax can delay the closing, so bring it up with the closing agent from day one. A cash buyer skips the lender's appraisal, but the title search still runs, so a clean tax record is what keeps the closing date firm.

Frequently asked questions

When does a Will County bill become late?

Delinquency begins after the later of June 1 or the printed date for the first installment, and after the later of September 1 or its printed date for the second. Interest then runs at 1.5% a month.

Where can I pay Will County tax face to face?

At the Treasurer's office inside the Will County Building, 302 N. Chicago Street, Joliet, which takes cash, checks and cards. A drop box at the building covers after-hours checks.

Can I contest my Will County assessment?

Yes, through a complaint to the Board of Review filed parcel by parcel. The window opens each August, and the Board's number is (815) 740-4707.

What is the Will County homestead cap?

Up to $8,000 off equalized assessed value, since Will borders Cook County. Owners 65 and older can take a separate senior exemption, also capped at $8,000.

What if my Will County taxes were sold?

You can still redeem by paying the County Clerk's tax redemption department before the period ends. Owners typically get one to three years, and the statute allows three years from the sale, with exceptions.

Williamson County, IL Property Tax Guide: Offices, Appeals and Selling With Tax Due

Cash Home Buyers in Illinois
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Williamson County, IL Property Tax Guide: inherited, behind on payments, tenants or repairs, we buy the house as-is
  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Williamson County, IL Property Tax Guide sale
  • Turn the Williamson County, IL Property Tax Guide offer down and you owe us nothing

Selling in Williamson County? Get a Cash Offer

We buy Williamson County houses as-is and reply with a written cash offer.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in Williamson County?
We buy Williamson County houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

Williamson County at a glance

Williamson County is in Southern Illinois. Marion is the county seat and the largest city, and Herrin, Carterville, Johnston City, Creal Springs and Hurst are the other towns. The 2020 census counted 67,153 residents in 28,145 households, and homeowners lived in roughly 69% of the occupied homes. Your bill depends on the school district, city and township your parcel sits in.

Storm damage comes up often here. The county has had serious tornado and derecho losses, so hail, wind and rebuild repairs show up on buyer inspections. Illinois also has a tax break for homes rebuilt after a disaster, covered under exemptions below.

Who handles the tax bill

Four offices touch the bill. Calling the right one saves a trip to the Administration Building at 407 N. Monroe Street in Marion.

  • The Supervisor of Assessments, Suite 205, keeps property records, takes exemption applications and runs the Board of Review paperwork. The office number is 618-998-2189.
  • The Board of Review rules on assessment complaints, and its clerk works out of the Supervisor's office.
  • The County Clerk files each taxing district's levy request and extends the tax to every parcel. Redemption after a tax sale also runs through the Clerk, at 618-998-2110.
  • The County Treasurer mails bills and collects. The counter is open weekdays from 8:00 am until 4:00 pm, and the phone is 618-998-2142.

The order of work is simple. The Supervisor and the Board of Review finish assessments, the Clerk extends the tax, and then the Treasurer sends the bill. The Treasurer only collects, so a bill that looks wrong is a question for the assessment office, not the collector.

Payment deadlines and options

The Treasurer sends one bill a year with two installment due dates. The dates change with each tax year. They are printed on the bill and posted on the Treasurer's collection schedule page, so read the stub before you plan a closing.

You can pay in any of these ways:

  • At most Williamson County banks, but only until the due date. After that, banks cannot collect and payment must be made at the Treasurer's office.
  • By mail, with an official U.S. postmark dated no later than the due date.
  • In person, including a night drop box.
  • Online with Visa, Mastercard, American Express, Discover or PayPal, or by phone at (618) 342-8470. The card company adds a convenience fee.

Enclose the installment stub so the right credit posts. Owners with several parcels can pay with one check if the parcel numbers are listed and each coupon is included. A canceled check serves as the receipt, or you can request an official one in writing. When an escrow account pays the tax, the county still mails you a copy for your records.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Williamson County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

How to contest your valuation

The complaint goes to the Williamson County Board of Review and is due 30 days from publication of the assessment list by the Supervisor of Assessments. Missing that window usually ends the appeal for the year. The one exception is wrong data the value was built on, such as incorrect square footage.

The Board's rules set the practical details:

  • Complaint forms are available only at the Supervisor's office on North Monroe Street, or by first-class mail on request. Faxed or emailed forms are rejected.
  • Allowed grounds are overvaluation, equity, physical data discrepancy and preferential assessment. Complaints about the amount of tax, a rate change or a percentage jump do not qualify.
  • All evidence goes in on paper with the complaint. Late evidence and evidence in other formats is not considered.
  • Anyone who bought after January 1, 2022 must disclose the price, date and whether the sale was arm's length.
  • Hearings run in 15-minute slots, in person or by teleconference, and written findings are mailed within 10 business days.

Assessments equal one-third of fair cash value, measured on a January 1 valuation date from sales in the three prior years. Appraisals must come from a state-certified appraiser. It helps to talk with the Supervisor's office before filing, but those talks do not move the deadline.

Homestead and other exemptions

Bring your tax statement to the Supervisor's office to apply for any of the programs below.

Homestead programs taken at the Williamson County assessment office
ExemptionWho qualifiesAmount or note
Owner OccupiedResident owner as of the assessment-year start; no age requirementProof of ownership and photo ID required
Homestead (senior)Owner-occupant turning or already 65 in the assessment yearProof of age and residence required
Senior Citizen Assessment Freeze65 or older, in the home since the prior assessment year, household income under the capCap changes over time; confirm with the office
Homestead ImprovementOwner-occupied, residential use onlyAdded value up to $75,000; apply before October 7 or within 30 days of the publication, whichever comes later
Disabled Veteran StandardService-connected rating of at least 30%$2,500 at 30% to 49%, $5,000 at 50% to 69%, tax exempt at 70% or more; annual filing
Returning VeteranVeteran home from active duty in an armed conflict$5,000 for two years
Disabled PersonsOwner who is 100% disabled, with proof$2,000; annual filing

A Natural Disaster Homestead Exemption also exists for a home rebuilt after storm, fire or flood damage. The structure must be rebuilt within two years, and the new square footage cannot exceed 110% of the original. If you are selling a rebuilt house, ask the assessment office whether it applies.

Owners should also look at their bill for the owner-occupied and senior credits. When a credit you qualify for is missing, call the Supervisor's office at 618-998-2189 to have it fixed.

When the tax goes unpaid

Each missed due date starts a penalty of 1.5% per month, and delinquent bills pick up a $10 certified-mail and advertising cost. Tax still unpaid after the second installment date is delinquent and heads to the county's annual tax sale, held in December.

At the sale the investor who bids the lowest interest rate pays the Treasurer the taxes, costs and fees. The county sells the unpaid tax, not the house. Records then pass to the County Clerk, and the owner or anyone with a financial interest has from 6 months to 2 1/2 years from the sale to redeem. The buyer may extend that to as much as three years. Redemption takes a single full payment in certified funds payable to the Williamson County Clerk, in person or by mail.

The cost grows over time. The bid rate applies to one six-month period and repeats every six months. Later years' taxes can be added at 12% per year, and if the buyer starts the tax deed process, the court can be petitioned for a deed once redemption lapses. Call the Clerk with the parcel number to get a redemption estimate.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Williamson County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Selling with taxes owed or due

The tax stays attached to the parcel, so an unpaid bill falls on the buyer unless the closing statement credits it. Look for a seller credit on that statement, or ask the closing attorney. Illinois bills a year behind, which means a sale in the fall usually leaves a bill for the year of sale still to come.

After the sale, forward any bill that arrives to the new owner. The Treasurer accepts no responsibility for a payment applied to the wrong bill, and a bill that never arrived still carries penalties.

Before closing, have the closing agent confirm three things:

  • Both installments of the latest bill are paid.
  • No earlier year sits with a tax buyer.
  • Any seller credit is written on the settlement statement.

If back taxes are on your parcel, get a redemption estimate from the County Clerk first. A cash sale to an as-is buyer can skip the repairs and showings, but the tax still has to be settled at the table, so know the number before you set a closing date.

Frequently asked questions

What is the deadline to appeal a Williamson County assessment?

Thirty days from publication of the assessment list. Talks with the assessment office do not extend that period, so file first.

Can I pay Williamson County property tax by credit card?

Yes. Online payment accepts Visa, Mastercard, American Express, Discover and PayPal, and a phone option exists at (618) 342-8470. A convenience fee from the card company applies.

Does Williamson County sell my house at the tax sale?

No. The December tax sale sells the unpaid tax to an investor, not the property. The owner keeps the right to redeem for at least six months and up to 2 1/2 years, and the buyer may extend that to three years.

Which office fixes a missing exemption on a Williamson County bill?

The Supervisor of Assessments, at 618-998-2189. Look for owner-occupied and senior credits on the bill and call that office when a qualifying credit is missing.

Who gets the tax bill after I sell in Williamson County?

The bill stays with the parcel. Settle it on the closing statement, get any seller credit in writing, and forward later bills to the new owner.

Selling in Winnebago County? Get a Cash Offer

Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in Winnebago County?

Winnebago County in brief

Rockford anchors Winnebago County, on the Wisconsin line in the Rock River valley. The 2020 count was 285,350 people in 115,459 households, and owners held 65.2% of occupied homes with renters in the other 34.8%. About 7.6% of housing units stood vacant. Loves Park and South Beloit are the other two cities.

Winters are hard on houses, and repairs found at inspection are a common reason an owner weighs a faster sale. The tax rules below decide what has to be settled before the deed changes hands.

Which offices deal with property tax

The work is divided among several desks, and a township assessor comes first in line. The county offices below share the building at 404 Elm Street in Rockford.

  • The Treasurer, Room 205, mails bills, takes payments and updates ownership after a deed is recorded. Call (815) 319-4400; the counter closes at 5 p.m. on weekdays.
  • The Supervisor of Assessments, Room 301, takes exemption applications at (815) 319-4460 and staffs the Board of Review.
  • The Board of Review, also Room 301, hears appeals at (815) 319-4463.
  • For taxes that an investor bought at the tax sale, the Treasurer refers owners to the County Clerk at (815) 319-4253.
  • Township assessors handle the first review of a value. Rockford Township's office is at 401 W. State Street, Suite 100, and Cherry Valley Township keeps a separate office on Blackhawk Road.

The 2026 notices put the median level of assessment at 30.01% in Rockford Township and 30.59% in Cherry Valley Township. Assessments are required by law to be equalized at 33.33% of fair market value.

Tax installments and payment methods

The Treasurer mails bills in early May and sets two installments, with the most recent set falling on June 12 and September 11. The calendar repeats yearly with a spring mailing and two installments, though the specific days shift.

Ways to pay:

  • Online or by phone at 815-859-9650. Check payments are free, while any card carries a 2.25% charge.
  • In the office, where the same card charge applies.
  • By mail to 404 Elm Street, Rm 205, Rockford, IL 61101. The PO box closed in 2024, so online banking bill-pay profiles need the street address.

Late installments pick up a 1.5% penalty for each month. Back taxes for 2024 and earlier cannot be paid online, and a year that an investor already bought goes through the County Clerk. On the final day before the tax sale, postmarks do not count: payment has to reach the office or be made online.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Winnebago County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

How to challenge your assessed value

Ask the township assessor for a review first. If that does not settle it, the next step is a filing with the Winnebago County Board of Review, reachable at (815) 319-4463. The filing cutoff falls in early September, and the date is printed on the yearly assessment notice. The Board's rules are on its county web page.

The notice gives owners a rough check: triple the total assessment and compare it with your own view of market value. A higher result than your estimate suggests over-assessment, and a lower one suggests under-assessment. The 2026 assessment feeds the bill payable in 2027.

Exemptions are subtracted from the equalized value, and the remainder is multiplied by the combined rate of every taxing body over the parcel. The appeal covers the value step only, so it cannot lower the rate.

Homestead exemptions and the senior freeze

File with the Supervisor of Assessments in Room 301. December 31 is the deadline for most homestead programs and July 1 for the senior freeze. The office lists these:

  • General Homestead: the increase in equalized value above its 1977 level, capped at $6,000, for a home the owner lives in. The office describes a one-time application.
  • Senior Citizens: a reduction of up to $5,000 for owners aged 65 and over.
  • Persons with Disabilities: up to $2,000 with documentation, renewed yearly.
  • Veteran with Disabilities: $2,500 at 30% to 49%, $5,000 at 50% to 69%, and up to $250,000 at 70% to 100%.
  • Returning Veteran: up to $5,000 for two consecutive years.
  • Homestead Improvement: up to $25,000 off taxable value for four years after new work, handled through the township assessor.

The Low-Income Senior Citizen Assessment Freeze has an income limit that a December 2025 state law, Public Act 104-0452, raises in steps:

Senior Assessment Freeze household income cap by tax year
Tax yearPayable inIncome year usedMaximum household income
202520262024$65,000
202620272025$75,000
202720282026$77,000
202820292027$79,000

After the 2028 year the limit stays at $79,000 unless lawmakers change it again. Current recipients get renewal forms by mail in early spring.

If a payment is missed

The Treasurer mails certified notices in late October with final amounts, since penalties change every 30 days, and names a final day to pay in early December to stay out of the annual tax sale. This year that day is Friday, December 4. A tax buyer then pays the bill and attaches a percentage rate.

The owner gets 2.5 years to redeem. Vacant non-farm land, buildings with seven or more residential units, and commercial or industrial property get one year. The certificate holder may extend the period, and the interest rate steps up every six months inside it, so an early payoff costs less. The Treasurer's page cites 35 ILCS 200/21-350 for the full rule.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Winnebago County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Settling tax before closing

Unpaid tax is a closing item. After the Recorder processes a deed, the Treasurer's office enters the buyer's information, and later bills carry the new name.

A checklist for the closing agent:

  • Which installments of the latest bill are paid, shown in the Treasurer's online account.
  • Whether any earlier year sits with a tax buyer. Those years cannot be paid online.
  • Any seller credit for the part of the year you owned the home, written on the settlement statement.
  • Exemptions: the homestead programs above require the owner to occupy the home.

If a bill is already delinquent, get the redemption figure from the County Clerk before you list, since the interest rate steps up every six months. A buyer who pays cash and takes the house as-is can close around these items, but the delinquent amount still comes out of your proceeds.

Recording the deed

Property tax and the deed meet at the Recorder's Office, Room 405 of the same administration building, at (815) 319-4325. A conveyance with consideration of $100 or more must arrive with an electronically completed transfer declaration from the state's MyDec portal, showing "Closing Completed," before the Recorder will accept it. Recording a compliant document costs $54.00 under the fee schedule that took effect January 1, 2025.

Owners can also enroll for free in the county's Property Fraud Alert, which sends a phone, email or text message whenever a document matching their name is recorded. It is handy if a house stays in your name for a while after closing, such as an inherited property. Fuller detail on fees and document rules is on the county's recorder of deeds page.

Frequently asked questions

When are Winnebago County tax installments due?

Bills go out in early May with two installments, most recently June 12 and September 11. The days shift a little each year. Late installments carry a 1.5% monthly penalty.

Does Winnebago County take cards for tax?

Yes, online, by phone at 815-859-9650 or at the counter, with a 2.25% charge on cards. Checks are free.

How long is redemption after a Winnebago County tax sale?

Generally 2.5 years. It is one year for vacant non-farm land, buildings of seven or more residential units, and commercial or industrial property, and the certificate holder may extend it.

When is the Winnebago County assessment complaint deadline?

It falls in early September and is printed on the yearly notice. Start with the township assessor, then go to the Board of Review at (815) 319-4463 if needed.

Where does the Winnebago County senior freeze application go?

To the Supervisor of Assessments, at (815) 319-4460, by July 1. Owners who already receive the freeze get renewal forms in the mail around March 1.

Woodford County, IL Property Tax Guide: Offices, Appeals and Selling With Tax Due

Cash Home Buyers in Illinois
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Woodford County, IL Property Tax Guide: inherited, behind on payments, tenants or repairs, we buy the house as-is
  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Woodford County, IL Property Tax Guide sale

Selling in Woodford County? Get a Cash Offer

We buy Woodford County houses as-is and reply with a written cash offer.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in Woodford County?
We buy Woodford County houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.

Woodford County in brief

Prairie, bluffs and cropland define Woodford County, part of the Peoria metro area. Eureka is the county seat. The 2020 census counted 38,467 people in 14,616 households, about 70% of residents live in rural areas, and owners live in 82.9% of occupied homes. Three places are legally cities: Eureka, El Paso and Minonk. Seventeen townships make up the county, and a 15-member elected board levies the county's own share of taxes.

Many sales here involve acreage or a divided farm tract, so parcel splits and farm appeals come up more than in a typical suburb. Both are covered below.

Offices that handle assessments and tax bills

Three offices sit inside the courthouse at 115 N. Main Street in Eureka, so a single visit can cover assessment, appeal and payment questions.

Woodford County property tax offices
OfficeRoleLocation and phone
Supervisor of AssessmentsOwner records, values, exemptions, parcel splits; does not calculate or collect taxRoom 101; 309-467-3708
Board of ReviewHears assessment appeals; clerk work is done in the assessment officeRoom 101; open weekdays 9 a.m. to 4 p.m.
County Treasurer and CollectorMails bills, collects, distributes to taxing districtsRoom 105; 309-467-4621

The assessment office answers for more than 25,000 parcels and aims for an accurate, uniform value on each. Homes, businesses and factories are assessed at 33 1/3% of market value, and a township-by-township comparison of sale prices with assessed values yields the yearly equalization factor.

On the collection side, the Treasurer mails over 25,000 real estate bills, collects more than $83 million and distributes it among over 102 taxing districts. The Supervisor of Assessments does not calculate taxes, set rates or collect them, so disputes over a parcel's value belong in the assessment office. If your neighborhood's assessment looks out of line, ask what the equalization factor is for your township.

Tax calendar and due dates

The Treasurer follows a pattern, not a fixed date. Mailing is usually in May, the first payment falls 30 days after that, and the second payment falls on the first Friday in September. One bill arrives with a payment coupon for each half.

Two other dates matter to sellers and buyers:

  • The yearly tax sale is held in late October.
  • Mobile home bills are mailed in March and are due 60 days after the mailing date.

Current and earlier bills can be looked up through the county's property tax search page, which helps a seller who has lost the paper copy. For the cost of a late payment or a redemption figure, call 309-467-4621, because those totals depend on the day you pay.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Woodford County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Appealing to the Board of Review

A window of 30 days opens when the assessment office prints that year's assessment changes in local newspapers. Values on a bill already in hand cannot be appealed, since that bill reflects the prior year. Arguments about tax dollars fail too, as the Board has no authority over district budgets.

What the Board's guidelines call for:

  • Owners of non-farm property complete PTAX-230 plus its addendum, and farm owners use PTAX-227 plus the farmland addendum.
  • Where buildings exist, state the land value and the improvement value separately.
  • Attach evidence for your view of fair cash value; an appraisal with supporting documentation qualifies.
  • Sign the appeal as owner and hand it to the Board's clerk in the assessment office.

The Board starts work by the first Monday in June, in Room 104 of the original courthouse building. Appellants get a mailed hearing time or a proposed action. Asking for a hearing on a proposed action takes a request within 10 days, and failing to show up for a noticed hearing can dismiss the appeal. A written decision is promised within 30 days of the hearing, and the final decision can go on to the Illinois Property Tax Appeal Board.

The Board may also issue a Certificate of Error for the previous assessment year until 5:00 p.m. on the day ahead of the tax sale. Duplicate assessments, arithmetic slips, improvements destroyed before the assessment date and a missed homestead exemption count as factual errors. Matters of judgment, including a building's quality grade, do not qualify.

Homestead exemptions

Every real property exemption runs through the assessment office. Applications and renewals come from that office, and the forms include:

  • The owner-occupied exemption form.
  • PTAX-324, the senior homestead exemption application.
  • PTAX-323, for home improvements.
  • PTAX-343 and PTAX-343-R, covering disabled persons with the physician's statement and renewal.
  • PTAX-342 and PTAX-342-R, the disabled veteran forms.
  • PTAX-330, for solar.

Property owned by governments and religious institutions follows the non-homestead path, using form PTAX-300. The Board adds its recommendation and the Department of Revenue has the last word. Because amounts and income limits shift with state law, call 309-467-3708 for current figures before pricing a house around a reduction.

Homestead exemptions are meant for people who own and live in the property, so a buyer moving in is the one to apply. The same office has forms for name and address changes, parcel splits and parcel consolidation.

If a bill goes unpaid

Delinquent parcels are offered at the late-October tax sale, where a buyer pays the unpaid tax. Illinois law sets the penalty and interest that build up and the time an owner has to redeem. The Treasurer can tell you where a parcel stands, and the County Clerk can quote redemption.

The sale also sets the cutoff for Certificates of Error. A factual mistake, such as an exemption that was never applied, can be fixed by the Board until the afternoon before the sale, so check a bill early. If you are about to list, look at the bill and the parcel record for errors first: a wrong owner, a missing exemption or a duplicate assessment is easier to fix before a buyer's lender sees it.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Woodford County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Handling the tax bill at closing

Begin with the parcel's payment status, then settle the year in progress on the closing statement. Bills arrive a year in arrears, so the September installment can cover a year the seller owned the house even after a spring or summer closing.

Before signing, check three things:

  • The parcel record shows both halves of the latest bill as paid.
  • The closing agent has prorated the current year and listed the credit on the settlement statement.
  • A divided farm or acreage tract has its parcel split request finished so the buyer's bill carries the right number.

Plan ahead if you are selling in the fall. The tax sale falls in late October, and a parcel that is behind can go to sale before a slow closing wraps up. A buyer who pays cash and closes fast can clear that risk, but you still need the Treasurer's payoff figure on the day you sign. If a mistake on the bill is the reason it is high, such as a missing owner-occupied exemption, get it corrected before the sale cutoff.

Frequently asked questions

What day is the second half payable in Woodford County?

The first Friday in September. The first half is payable 30 days after the usual May mailing.

What is the filing window for a Woodford County assessment appeal?

Thirty days, counted from the date the assessment office publishes the year's changes in local newspapers. The values on a bill you already hold are not open to appeal.

Who works out the tax amount in Woodford County?

Not the Supervisor of Assessments, which handles values and exemptions only. The taxing districts' levies set the amount, and the Treasurer collects.

Is a Woodford County Board of Review ruling final?

No. A notice of final decision may be appealed to the Illinois Property Tax Appeal Board.

What month is the Woodford County tax sale?

Late October. Mobile home bills run on their own schedule: mailed in March, payable 60 days afterward.
